title: Central nervous system efficacy of third generation vs. first generation EGFR-TKIs in the first line treatment for EGFR-mutated non-small cell lung cancer with central nervous system metastases: a systematic review and meta-analysis of phase 3 randomized controlled trials.
authors: Gan J, Zhu S, Fang Y et al.
abstract:
BACKGROUND: Epidermal growth factor receptor (EGFR)-mutant non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC) with central nervous system (CNS) metastases poses significant treatment challenges, as first-generation EGFR-tyrosine kinase inhibitors (TKIs) (FGET) show limited CNS efficacy. Although third-generation EGFR-TKIs (TGET) exhibit superior CNS penetration, the optimal choice for first-line treatment remains debated. This meta-analysis aims to resolve this controversy by directly comparing the CNS efficacy of TGET vs. FGET in patients with EGFR-mutant NSCLC and CNS metastases.
METHODS: A thorough literature search was performed for phase 3 randomized controlled trials (RCTs) comparing TGET and FGET in patients with EGFR-mutated NSCLC and CNS metastases. The primary outcome was CNS-progression-free survival (PFS), and secondary outcomes included overall survival (OS), PFS, CNS response rates, and adverse events (AEs). The study was registered in PROSPERO (ID: CRD42024629581).
RESULTS: A total of 5 phase 3 RCTs (AENEAS, FLAURA, FURLONG, IBIO-103, and LASER301) met the inclusion criteria. TGET demonstrated superior efficacy in CNS-PFS [hazard ratio (HR): 0.44 (0.33, 0.58), P<0.001], PFS [HR: 0.44 (0.35, 0.54), P<0.001], CNS-objective response rate (ORR) [risk ratio (RR): 1.32 (1.15, 1.52), P<0.001], CNS-complete response (CR) [RR: 3.40 (1.39, 8.28), P=0.007], and CNS-duration of response (DOR) [HR: 0.39 (0.21, 0.73), P=0.003]. The CNS-PFS rate at 4-24 months and PFS at 10-24 months were significantly higher in the TGET group. OS data were available from only 2 of the 5 included phase 3 RCTs. In this analysis, OS numerically favored the TGET group but did not reach statistical significance [HR: 0.79 (0.55, 1.13), P=0.20]. At the cutoff time, more CNS progressions were found in the FGET [RR: 0.59 (0.44, 0.80), P=0.001]. Additionally, less grade 3-5 treatment-related AEs (TRAEs) were found in the TGET group [RR: 0.67 (0.46, 0.98), P=0.04].
CONCLUSIONS: TGET appeared to be better than FGET for patients with EGFR-mutated NSCLC and CNS metastases, showing improved survival, CNS efficacy, and safety.

title: Tumor-associated macrophages beyond M1/M2 in NSCLC: spatially organized programs, therapy resistance, and translational targeting.
authors: Wang XL, Jiang Z, Lu Q et al.
abstract: Tumor-associated macrophages (TAMs) are abundant and functionally diverse components of the lung tumor microenvironment (TME) and are associated with therapeutic response and resistance in non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC). Durable responses to immune checkpoint inhibitors (ICIs) and targeted therapies remain limited, with TAM-associated immune evasion and therapy-refractory microenvironments representing potentially relevant components of this resistance landscape. This narrative review prioritizes evidence from human NSCLC specimens and clinically annotated cohorts, especially from single-cell RNA sequencing (scRNA-seq) and spatial transcriptomics, while integrating relevant mechanistic evidence from NSCLC experimental systems, animal models, and related cancer contexts. Moving beyond the M1/M2 paradigm, we synthesize convergent findings to describe recurring, niche-resolved TAM programs. Across NSCLC, we highlight recurrent SPP1-associated, TREM2-associated, and C1q/LAM-like macrophage programs as a practical framework for integrating recurrent TAM states across spatial and treatment contexts. We propose an integrative framework in which TAM state dynamics are associated with, and may contribute to, therapy-refractory phenotypes during (i) ICI therapy through immune exclusion, (ii) oncogene-targeted therapy through macrophage-associated bypass signaling and survival plasticity, particularly in EGFR-TKI resistance, and (iii) post-radiochemotherapy microenvironmental remodeling, with potential implications for residual disease ecosystems that require further clinical validation, particularly with respect to recurrence and relapse. TAM program signatures and spatial organization provide a rationale for investigating biomarker-guided stratification and macrophage-directed combination strategies targeting state-niche axes. Future work should prioritize clinically validated, state- and niche-resolved multimodal biomarkers and prospective translational studies to support rational pairing with ICIs and targeted therapies.

title: Optimizing Lung-molGPA-Directed Therapy for EGFR/ALK/ROS1-Wildtype Non-Small Cell Lung Cancer Brain Metastases: Survival Outcomes Analysis.
authors: Feng B, Yang D, Yang X et al.
abstract: Patients with non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC) and brain metastases whose tumors lack EGFR, ALK, or ROS1 alterations have heterogeneous outcomes and limited evidence to guide treatment intensity. We assessed whether Lung-molGPA could stratify prognosis and inform treatment selection in this population. This retrospective two-center cohort included 811 patients with EGFR/ALK/ROS1-wild-type NSCLC treated between September 2013 and August 2022. Overall survival (OS) was evaluated using Kaplan-Meier methods and center-stratified multivariable Cox regression across three Lung-molGPA strata and treatment modalities. Median OS was 6.9 months (95% confidence interval [CI], 6.4-7.4) overall and 4.81 (4.20-5.30), 7.65 (6.73-8.40), and 16.00 (13.40-22.90) months in the Lung-molGPA 0-1.0, 1.5-2.0, and 2.5-3.0 groups, respectively (p < 0.001). Compared with the 0-1.0 group, adjusted mortality was lower in the 1.5-2.0 (hazard ratio [HR], 0.68; 95% CI, 0.58-0.80) and 2.5-3.0 groups (HR, 0.39; 95% CI, 0.30-0.50). Chemotherapy, immunotherapy, antiangiogenic therapy, and brain- and chest-directed local therapy were independently associated with lower mortality, although their associations varied across prognostic strata and treatment contexts. Lung-molGPA provides clinically meaningful prognostic separation and may help tailor treatment intensity for EGFR/ALK/ROS1-wild-type NSCLC with brain metastases.

title: Surgical resection for indeterminate pulmonary nodules in patients with prior breast cancer: diagnostic value and biomarker reassessment.
authors: Masuda Y, Ono S, Tanaka M et al.
abstract:
BACKGROUND: Pulmonary nodules detected during postoperative surveillance in breast cancer survivors present a diagnostic challenge because imaging findings alone often cannot reliably distinguish pulmonary metastases from primary lung cancer. Surgical resection provides definitive pathological diagnosis while simultaneously enabling biomarker reassessment in metastatic lesions. This study evaluated the diagnostic value and clinical significance of pulmonary resection for indeterminate pulmonary nodules in patients with prior breast cancer.
METHODS: We retrospectively reviewed 33 pulmonary resections performed in 32 consecutive patients with a history of breast cancer who underwent pulmonary resection for indeterminate pulmonary nodules between 2016 and 2025. Clinicopathological findings, imaging characteristics, perioperative outcomes, and receptor discordance between primary breast tumors and pulmonary metastatic lesions were analyzed. Paired biomarker data were available for 18 patients with pulmonary metastases.
RESULTS: Final pathological diagnoses included metastatic breast cancer in 23 lesions (69.7%), primary lung cancer in 9 lesions (27.3%), and benign disease in 1 lesion (3.0%), indicating that more than one-quarter of lesions suspected preoperatively to represent pulmonary metastases were actually primary lung cancers. Most procedures were performed using video-assisted thoracoscopic surgery (87.9%). Among patients with paired biomarker data, substantial discordance in hormone receptor and human epidermal growth factor receptor 2 (HER2) expression was observed, including frequent conversion between HER2-0 and HER2-low categories. Biomarker reassessment resulted in modification of subsequent systemic treatment in three patients. Perioperative outcomes were favorable, with no operative mortality and low postoperative morbidity.
CONCLUSIONS: Surgical resection for indeterminate pulmonary nodules in selected patients with prior breast cancer provides definitive pathological diagnosis, appropriate local treatment, and sufficient tissue for biomarker reassessment. Histological confirmation should be considered when imaging findings remain inconclusive because pulmonary nodules in breast cancer survivors are not necessarily metastatic disease. Biomarker reassessment may directly influence individualized systemic treatment strategies in the HER2-low era.

title: Clinical outcomes and prognostic factors of Ommaya reservoir-based intrathecal chemotherapy in lung cancer leptomeningeal metastasis: a retrospective cohort study.
authors: Yang Y, Feng M, Ong YX et al.
abstract:
OBJECTIVES: To evaluate clinical outcomes and identify prognostic determinants in patients with lung cancer leptomeningeal metastasis (LCLM) treated with Ommaya reservoir-based intrathecal (IT) chemotherapy.
METHOD: We retrospectively reviewed 154 LCLM patients treated at Fudan University Shanghai Cancer Center (2022-2025). All patients underwent Ommaya reservoir implantation, or combined with VP shunt. IT pemetrexed (30 mg/week) was delivered for 4-6 consecutive weeks. Clinical characteristics, cerebrospinal fluid (CSF) and magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) features were collected. Survival outcomes were assessed using Kaplan-Meier and Cox regression analyses.
RESULTS: The cohort had a median age of 59 years (IQR, 53-65) with predominance of female sex (59.1%), lung adenocarcinoma (98.1%), and EGFR mutations (76.7%). Median overall survival (OS) for the entire cohort was 331 days (IQR, 266-446). To provide guidance on clinical decision making, we established an exploratory four-tier prognostic system integrating KPS and intracranial pressure (ICP), categorizing patients into distinct prognostic quartiles. Our analysis revealed that among patients with Karnofsky Performance Status (KPS) ≥70, a normal ICP was associated with superior survival. Conversely, in patients with KPS ≤ 50, a decrease in intracranial pressure indicates a poorer prognosis for the patients. Multivariate Cox regression identified KPS, extracranial metastasis, MRI morphology, and CSF glucose/protein as independent prognostic factors. A nomogram developed from these variables showed excellent discrimination (AUC = 0.894) and robust calibration.
CONCLUSIONS: This study establishes a practical risk stratification system and a prognostic nomogram to assist individualized clinical decision-making for LCLM patients.

title: Targeting the Tumor Microenvironment Network to Overcome Immunotherapy Resistance in Non-Small Cell Lung Cancer: Mechanisms to Clinical Translation.
authors: Wang Z, Luo Z, Wang L et al.
abstract:
BACKGROUND: Immunotherapy has transformed the treatment landscape for advanced non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC), yet resistance mediated by the tumor microenvironment (TME) limits its efficacy in most patients. This review aims to synthesize the current understanding of the TME as an integrated network driving immunotherapy resistance and to evaluate emerging therapeutic strategies aimed at overcoming it.
METHODS: We conducted a comprehensive narrative review of key literature in the field, sourced from PubMed and major conference proceedings. The focus was on mechanistic studies elucidating immunosuppressive cell circuits, metabolic reprogramming, epigenetic regulation, spatial heterogeneity, and microbiome interactions within the lung cancer TME. Preclinical and clinical evidence for TME-targeted combination therapies and biomarker development was also critically analyzed.
RESULTS: The TME orchestrates resistance through highly interconnected axes: (1) cellular circuits including myeloid-derived suppressor cells (MDSCs), regulatory T cells (Tregs), and M2-polarized tumor-associated macrophages (M2-TAMs), (2) metabolic barriers (lactate acidosis, nutrient depletion), (3) epigenetic reprogramming, and (4) systemic communication via exosomes and the microbiome. Spatial transcriptomics reveals that driver mutations (e.g., EGFR, KRAS) shape distinct immune-excluded architectures. To disrupt this network, rational combination strategies-such as immune checkpoint inhibitors with metabolic modulators (LDHAi), epigenetic drugs, targeted agents (METi), or microbiome interventions-show synergistic potential in early-phase trials. Furthermore, a tiered biomarker system integrating spatial, metabolic, and microbial features is proposed to guide patient stratification.
CONCLUSION: Overcoming immunotherapy resistance requires a paradigm shift from single-target to network-targeted therapy. This review provides an integrated framework for understanding TME-mediated resistance and translates these insights into a roadmap for clinical translation. Future efforts must prioritize biomarker-validated, rationally designed combination therapies to improve outcomes for patients with resistant NSCLC.

title: First-line treatment outcomes in HER2-altered advanced NSCLC: a real-world multi-center study comparing trastuzumab deruxtecan with conventional therapies and analysis by HER2/EGFR co-alteration status.
authors: Liu C, Li T, Qin BY et al.
abstract:
BACKGROUND: First-line treatment options for HER2-altered advanced non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC) remain limited, especially in cases with HER2-EGFR co-alterations. While new agents like trastuzumab deruxtecan (T-DXd) have emerged, its real-world evidence in first line remains limited.
METHODS: This study included patients with advanced NSCLC who had HER2 mutations or amplification and received first-line systemic therapy at six medical centers. Outcomes were evaluated following chemotherapy-based combinations, pan-HER tyrosine kinase inhibitors (TKIs), and T-DXd. Endpoints included progression-free survival (PFS), objective response rate (ORR), disease control rate (DCR), one-year and two-year survival rates, and toxicity.
RESULTS: A total of 69 patients were enrolled, comprising 45 with only HER2 alterations and 24 with HER2-EGFR co-alterations. In patients with only HER2-altered NSCLC, those receiving first-line T-DXd had an mPFS of 15.7 months (95% CI, 12.5-18.9), an ORR of 85.7%, and a DCR of 100.0%. The mPFS for patients receiving chemotherapy-based regimens, pan-HER TKIs, and chemotherapy plus pan-HER TKIs were 7.6 (95% CI, 6.6-8.5) months, 4.4 (95% CI, 4.0-4.9) months, and 7.0 (95% CI, 6.1-9.1) months, respectively. The ORR for the three groups above was 33.3%, 0, and 0, respectively. In subgroup analysis, patients with only HER2 alterations who did not harbor TP53 mutations had a longer PFS than those with TP53 co-mutations (8.7 m vs. 7.2 m; HR: 0.35; 95% CI: 0.11-0.99; P = 0.048). In patients with EGFR-HER2 co-alterations, first-line EGFR-TKI monotherapy yielded an mPFS of 9.7 (95% CI, 8.6-10.8) months, an ORR of 40.0%, and a DCR of 93.3%. Regarding safety, we did not observe Grade ≥ 3 TRAEs in first-line T-DXd treatment.
CONCLUSIONS: First-line T-DXd showed promising activity signals in only HER2-altered NSCLC. In EGFR-HER2 co-altered patients, the EGFR-TKI monotherapy showed limited efficacy. The findings underscored the urgent need for prospective randomised trials.

title: DYT8 drives lung adenocarcinoma through EGFR-mediated PSMC6 recruitment and uncharacterized phosphorylation at Ser 306 and 525 of c-Src.
authors: Cai ML, Wang MY, Zhao XJ et al.
abstract: Lung adenocarcinoma (LUAD) is a multi-kinase hyperactivation-driven malignancy. Targeted therapies are effective but have limited application, primarily due to a small eligible patient population and the development of drug resistance. Analysis of TCGA and tissue microarray show that Dystonia 8 (DYT8) is specially highly expressed in more than 70% of LUAD patients. Furthermore, increased DYT8 expression is positively associated with tumor malignancy and negatively associated with survival. Using the Dyt8 knock-in (cKrasLSL-G12D/+p53R172H/+-Dyt8-KI) and knockout (cKrasLSL-G12D/+p53R172H/+-Dyt8-KO) transgenic mice, we identify DYT8 as key activator that accelerates the initiation and progression of LUAD. Mechanistically, EGFR-mediated phosphorylation of DYT8 at Y120 reinforces its stability by increasing its interaction with PSMC6, a protein that is highly expressed in LUAD and associated with an unfavorable prognosis. DYT8 drives LUAD malignant transformation by activating Src. Although Y419 phosphorylation is a recognized key event in Src-driven LUAD, our study identifies novel phosphorylation sties at S306 and S525 that are activated by DYT8, which these novel sites being more critical for DYT8-driven malignant transformation than Y419 phosphorylation. Furthermore, the knockdown of Dyt8 rescues EGFR-triggered carcinogenesis and resistance to EGFR tyrosine kinase inhibitors (EGFR-TKIs). These findings reveal that DYT8 drives LUAD via a previously unreported Src activation mechanism and identify EGFR-DYT8-PSMC6 axis as the key determinant of high DYT8 level, thereby conferring a novel therapeutic strategy for wider LUAD patients, including those with EGFR-TKIs resistant.

title: Comparative efficacy of uniportal and multiportal robotic-assisted thoracoscopic surgery for non-small cell lung cancer: a systematic review and meta-analysis.
authors: He Z, Wan Z, Hu Y
abstract:
BACKGROUND: Currently, the comparative efficacy of different robotic surgical systems in the treatment of lung cancer remains unclear. This study aimed to systematically evaluate the differences in efficacy between uniportal robotic-assisted thoracoscopic surgery (URATS) and multiportal robotic-assisted thoracoscopic surgery (MRATS) for the treatment of non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC).
METHODS: PubMed, Cochrane Library, Web of Science, and Embase were searched from database inception to March 2026 following standardized retrieval procedures. Two authors independently performed literature retrieval, preliminary screening, full-text reassessment, raw data extraction, and cross-checking. The Newcastle-Ottawa Scale (NOS) was used to assess the quality of the included studies, and all statistical analyses were performed using Stata 17.0. This study has been registered on the INPLASY platform (protocol registration number: INPLASY202670008).
RESULTS: Nine studies involving 1,827 patients were ultimately included. NOS assessment indicated that all included studies were of moderate-to-high quality. The pooled meta-analysis showed that, compared with MRATS, URATS was associated with a longer operative time [weighted mean difference (WMD) =14.70, 95% confidence interval (95% CI): 6.06-23.35, P=0.04, I2=24.5%] but a shorter length of hospital stay (WMD =-1.07, 95% CI: -1.36 to -0.77), P<0.01, I2=43.3%). No significant differences were observed in 1-year all-cause mortality, infection, air leak, hemothorax, duration of chest tube drainage, intraoperative blood loss, or number of dissected lymph nodes.
CONCLUSIONS: Compared with MRATS, URATS for NSCLC was associated with a longer operative time but a shorter hospital stay, while no statistically significant differences were observed in the other assessed outcomes. These findings suggest that URATS may be a feasible minimally invasive surgical approach for NSCLC, although further prospective studies are warranted.

title: Perioperative analgesic strategies for video-assisted thoracoscopic lobectomy: a systematic review and meta-analysis.
authors: Kadier A, Du X
abstract:
BACKGROUND: Video-assisted thoracoscopic surgery (VATS) lobectomy is the standard of care for early-stage lung cancer, yet 20-30% of patients still experience moderate-to-severe acute postoperative pain. A wide range of perioperative analgesic strategies-regional blocks, systemic adjuncts, cryoanalgesia, and multimodal combinations-have been evaluated, but their comparative effects on clinically meaningful endpoints such as postoperative complications remain uncertain. The aim of this systematic review and meta-analysis was to evaluate the comparative efficacy and safety of perioperative analgesic strategies for VATS lobectomy.
METHODS: We conducted a systematic review and meta-analysis of randomised controlled trials (RCTs) (PROSPERO CRD420251186565), following the PRISMA 2020 statement. PubMed/MEDLINE and Web of Science Core Collection were searched from 1 January 2010 to 26 June 2026. Two reviewers independently screened records, extracted data, and assessed risk of bias using the Cochrane Risk of Bias 2 (RoB 2) tool per outcome. Postoperative complications were pooled as risk ratios (RR) with 95% confidence intervals (CIs) using a random-effects model with restricted maximum-likelihood (REML) estimation. Studies were grouped by intervention type for subgroup analysis. Sensitivity was assessed with leave-one-out analysis.
RESULTS: Seven trials (n=505) met inclusion criteria. The evidence base was clinically heterogeneous: included comparisons encompassed regional technique variations [paravertebral block (PVB), serratus anterior plane block (SAPB), intercostal nerve block (ICNB), and their combinations], systemic adjunctive analgesics (nefopam), and intercostal cryoanalgesia. Only three trials reported usable complication data for quantitative synthesis (n=245). The overall pooled RR for postoperative complications was 0.84 (95% CI: 0.65-1.08; P=0.18), but this estimate was dominated by a single trial (Koliakos 2025, 75.2% weight). Between-study heterogeneity was absent (I2=0%, τ2=0; Q=0.39, df =2, P=0.82). Subgroup analyses by intervention class (regional techniques, systemic adjuncts, cryoanalgesia) did not yield statistically significant pooled estimates. Leave-one-out exclusion of the largest study shifted the point estimate to RR 0.95 (95% CI: 0.57-1.58), confirming strong dependence on a single trial. With fewer than 10 studies, formal publication bias assessment was not performed.
CONCLUSIONS: The available evidence on perioperative analgesic strategies for VATS lobectomy consists of small, heterogeneous trials comparing diverse interventions. No single strategy has been shown to consistently reduce postoperative complications. The evidence base is insufficient to guide clinical practice. Adequately powered, multicentre RCTs with standardised interventions, composite complication endpoints, and extended follow-up are needed.

title: Multifocal ground-glass opacities in lung cancer: a narrative review of genomic evolution, immune ecology, and biology-informed clinical management.
authors: Li X, Li Y, Jiang J et al.
abstract:
BACKGROUND AND OBJECTIVE: Ground-glass opacity (GGO) is a computed tomography descriptor rather than a histologic diagnosis. Multifocal GGOs (mGGOs) are increasingly detected during lung cancer screening, yet their clonal origins, immune ecology, progression risk, and optimal management remain difficult to reconcile within conventional lung cancer frameworks. This narrative review evaluates genomic, immunologic, and clinical evidence relevant to mGGOs and examines how biological findings may inform surveillance and local treatment without encouraging overtreatment.
METHODS: PubMed/MEDLINE, Web of Science, Google Scholar, and selected guideline and trial sources were searched through 29 July 2026 for English-language studies published mainly from January 2020 to July 2026, supplemented by earlier landmark reports. Search concepts included mGGO, subsolid nodule, synchronous multiple primary lung cancer (SMPLC), clonality, single-cell and spatial transcriptomics (ST), immune microenvironment, active surveillance, and parenchyma-sparing surgery.
KEY CONTENT AND FINDINGS: Many mGGO presentations are compatible with clonally independent synchronous primaries, although intrapulmonary metastasis (IPM) can occur and developmental mosaicism remains a single-study, selected-patient hypothesis. Early lesions may have low mutational burden and attenuated effector activity, but immunoediting, regulatory T-cell enrichment, dysfunctional CD8-positive T-cell states, and inhibitory non-classical antigen-presentation pathways can already be present in adenocarcinoma in situ or minimally invasive adenocarcinoma. We therefore use relative adaptive immune quiescence as a descriptive population-level term, not as evidence of absent immune pressure. Prospective ECTOP-1021 data support short-term feasibility of surveillance in a highly selected cohort, but do not establish comparative effectiveness.
CONCLUSIONS: A biology-informed framework can refine risk discussion for selected patients with mGGOs, provided that radiologic terms are not treated as histologic diagnoses and mechanistic associations are not converted into clinical recommendations. Surveillance, local treatment, and parenchyma preservation should remain multidisciplinary and evidence-calibrated; biomarker-guided triage and interception strategies require prospective GGO-specific validation.

title: Diagnosis and selection of surgical approaches for synchronous multiple primary lung cancer: a narrative review.
authors: Huang K, Tang J
abstract:
BACKGROUND AND OBJECTIVE: Synchronous multiple primary lung cancer (SMPLC) is a distinct clinical entity in lung cancer management. Because SMPLC differs substantially from intrapulmonary metastasis (IPM) in staging, treatment strategy, and prognosis, accurate assessment of the clonal relationship among multiple malignant pulmonary lesions is essential for treatment planning. This narrative review summarizes the diagnostic basis, preoperative assessment, and selection of surgical approaches for SMPLC and discusses bilateral surgery, residual ground-glass nodules, and future research directions.
METHODS: PubMed was searched for English- or Chinese-language publications from 1 January 2000 to 18 August 2026 using terms related to SMPLC, IPM, molecular clonality, lobectomy, segmentectomy, wedge resection, bilateral surgery, subsolid nodules, and local therapy. An updated search was performed during revision to capture recent literature on molecular clonality, bilateral video-assisted thoracoscopic surgery (VATS), and residual ground-glass nodules. Relevant guidelines, reviews, cohort studies, systematic reviews, case series, and representative case reports were selected according to their relevance to the clinical scope of this review. No formal risk-of-bias assessment or quantitative synthesis was performed.
KEY CONTENT AND FINDINGS: Traditional diagnosis is based mainly on lesion distribution and histologic features, but morphology alone has limitations when lesions share similar histologic types. Comprehensive histologic assessment, thin-section computed tomography, and selective molecular testing provide complementary evidence for differentiating SMPLC from IPM. Surgery remains the principal treatment for resectable SMPLC. The choice among lobectomy, anatomical segmentectomy, wedge resection, and combined resection should consider the invasiveness of the dominant and secondary lesions, the number and distribution of lesions, laterality, nodal status, predicted postoperative pulmonary function, comorbidity, and cumulative loss of lung parenchyma. In carefully selected patients with early-stage disease, parenchyma-sparing strategies may provide acceptable oncologic outcomes; however, current evidence is derived mainly from retrospective studies and is limited by selection bias and heterogeneous diagnostic criteria.
CONCLUSIONS: Accurate multidisciplinary diagnosis and individualized surgical planning are central to SMPLC management. Prospective multicenter studies using standardized diagnostic criteria are needed to clarify the optimal extent of resection, timing of bilateral surgery, and management of residual low-risk ground-glass nodules.

title: Immune checkpoint inhibitors across neoadjuvant, perioperative, and adjuvant settings for resectable non-small-cell lung cancer: a systematic review and meta-analysis of randomized trials.
authors: Dai J, Liu M, Li H et al.
abstract:
BACKGROUND: Randomized evidence for immune checkpoint inhibition in resectable non-small-cell lung cancer has progressed from pathological response to mature survival outcomes. We examined exploratory directional alignment across endpoints and quantified clinical yield, treatment burden, and the extent of perioperative therapy delivery.
METHODS: We synthesized 20 peer-reviewed reports from 12 parent randomized trials, including 8,197 unique participants and 13 eligible randomized treatment comparisons. The parent trial was the analysis unit, and the latest compatible report replaced earlier estimates for each time-to-event outcome. Direct randomized comparisons were pooled using restricted maximum-likelihood random-effects models. We reconstructed cumulative event-free survival (EFS) and overall survival (OS) evidence, estimated absolute differences, performed exploratory trial-level cross-endpoint analyses, and pooled the proportion of experimental-arm patients who started postoperative study treatment.
RESULTS: Across seven trials, treatment initiated before surgery reduced EFS events by 41% (HR, 0.59; 95% CI: 0.53-0.66; I2 = 12%). Five trials showed a 32% reduction in death (HR, 0.68; 95% CI: 0.58-0.80; I2 = 0%). Per 100 randomized patients, preoperative-start therapy produced 31 additional major pathological responses (95% CI: 24-39), 22 additional pathological complete responses (95% CI: 16-27), and 4 additional patients who underwent or attempted curative-intent surgery (95% CI: 1-7). Grade ≥3 treatment-related adverse events increased by approximately 4 per 100 patients (95% CI: 0-8). In exploratory analyses, larger pCR improvements tended to accompany lower EFS HRs (Spearman ρ = -0.67; p = 0.098; k = 7), and EFS and OS estimates were directionally aligned (ρ = 0.95; p = 0.051; k = 4). In six perioperative trials, 69.7% (95% CI: 65.5%-73.7%) of randomized experimental-arm patients started postoperative study treatment.
CONCLUSION: ICI-containing strategies initiated before surgery improve pathological response, EFS, and OS in resectable NSCLC. Approximately 70% of patients assigned to perioperative experimental arms started postoperative study treatment; this descriptive treatment-delivery finding does not establish whether postoperative ICI can be safely omitted. Prospective response- and residual-risk-guided randomized trials are required.

title: Green Spectrofluorimetric Strategies for Capmatinib and Curcumin Determination.
authors: El-Sharkasy ME, Elmansi H, Belal F et al.
abstract: The growing convergence between precision oncology and natural-product-based therapeutics has fostered innovative strategies that integrate molecularly targeted anticancer agents with biologically active phytochemicals to enhance therapeutic efficacy and overcome treatment resistance. Capmatinib, a selective MET inhibitor approved for MET-driven non-small cell lung cancer, and curcumin, a natural polyphenol possessing antioxidant, anti-inflammatory, and anticancer activities, represent a promising therapeutic combination. This emerging paradigm highlights the need for sensitive, sustainable, and efficient analytical platforms capable of monitoring both compounds in pharmaceutical and biological matrices. Accordingly, two new spectrofluorimetric methods were created and validated, allowing for the quantification of capmatinib and the simultaneous assay of capmatinib-curcumin combinations. The first method harnessed the unique microenvironmental properties of sodium dodecyl sulfate as a monomeric denaturant to markedly enhance the intrinsic fluorescence of capmatinib in an aqueous medium, providing a linear response over 5.0-120.0 ng/mL with a detection limit of 1.42 ng/mL. The second method exploited synchronous spectrofluorimetry (Δλ = 160 nm) to resolve overlapping fluorescence signals, enabling separation-free quantification of capmatinib and curcumin across concentration ranges of 20.0-700.0 and 10.0-250.0 ng/mL, respectively. Both methods demonstrated excellent selectivity, accuracy, and precision according to ICH guidelines and were successfully applied to spiked human plasma samples.

title: The Association Between CD40 rs1883832 Polymorphism and Cancer Susceptibility: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis.
authors: Wang B, Gao M, Fan S et al.
abstract: The CD40 gene, a key immune regulatory molecule, has been implicated in tumorigenesis, and its functional polymorphism rs1883832 located in the Kozak sequence, may modulate cancer susceptibility by influencing CD40 expression. To clarify inconsistent epidemiological findings, a comprehensive meta-analysis was conducted to evaluate the association between the CD40 rs1883832 polymorphism and overall cancer risk. Eligible case-control studies were systematically identified from PubMed, Web of Science and Cochrane Library up to August 15, 2025, and pooled odds ratios (OR) with 95% confidence intervals (CI) were calculated under five genetic models. Eight studies encompassing 3858 cancer cases and 4699 controls met the inclusion criteria. The results revealed a significant association between the rs1883832 T allele and elevated cancer risk in 4 multiple models, including the allele (T vs. C: OR = 1.26, 95% CI: 1.09-1.47, p < 0.01), homozygous (TT vs. CC: OR = 1.58, 95% CI: 1.16-2.16, p < 0.01), recessive (TT vs. TC + CC: OR = 1.43, 95% CI: 1.18-1.82, p < 0.01), and dominant (TT + TC vs. CC: OR = 1.29, 95% CI: 1.03-1.62, p = 0.03) models. Subgroup analyses revealed suggestive patterns of associations in lung cancer and Asian populations. Sensitivity analyses confirmed the robustness of these findings, and no substantial publication bias was detected. In conclusion, this meta-analysis provides compelling evidence that the CD40 rs1883832 T allele may confer increased susceptibility to cancer, thereby underscoring the potential influence of immune gene polymorphisms in carcinogenesis and their relevance for genetic risk assessment in oncology. Trial Registration: PROSPERO number: CRD420251130223.

title: Prophylactic high-flow nasal oxygen vs. conventional oxygen for prevention of postoperative respiratory complications: a randomized trial.
authors: Lin R, Huang Y, Yu G et al.
abstract:
BACKGROUND: Postoperative pulmonary complications (PPCs) are a major cause of morbidity after lung resection, particularly in older adults. Following extubation, noninvasive respiratory support strategies are increasingly used to prevent respiratory deterioration, but the role of prophylactic high-flow nasal cannula (HFNC) in this setting remains uncertain.
METHODS: In this single-center, open-label randomized controlled trial, patients undergoing video-assisted thoracoscopic surgery (VATS) lobectomy or segmentectomy for stage I-IIIa non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC) were randomized to HFNC or conventional oxygen therapy (COT). The primary outcome was PPC severity during hospitalization, analyzed using ordinal logistic regression; the incidence of clinically relevant PPCs (grade ≥ 2) was also compared between groups. Secondary outcomes included longitudinal respiratory symptoms (mMRC, LCQ-MC, sCSS) and symptom-related functional interference (MDASI-LC), analyzed using mixed-effects models.
RESULTS: A total of 210 patients were included in the modified intention-to-treat analysis (HFNC, n = 104; COT, n = 106). HFNC reduced PPC severity (ordinal OR, 0.50; 95% CI, 0.28-0.91; P = 0.022) and moderate-to-severe PPCs (23.1% vs. 39.6%; absolute risk difference, -15.6%; 95% CI, -28.0% to -3.2%; P = 0.010). HFNC was associated with a lower burden of clinically relevant PPCs. Secondary analyses also suggested improvements in early postoperative respiratory symptoms and symptom-related functional interference. Secondary analyses also suggested improvements in early postoperative respiratory symptoms and symptom-related functional interference. No differences were observed in physiological outcomes or length of stay.
CONCLUSION: In older adults undergoing lung resection, prophylactic HFNC reduced in-hospital PPC burden and was associated with more favorable early postoperative respiratory recovery. These findings suggest that prophylactic HFNC may provide benefit as a potential preventive respiratory support option in selected older or higher-risk postoperative patients, although routine prophylactic use in all patients undergoing lung resection is not supported by the present findings.
TRIAL REGISTRATION: This study was approved by the Chinese Clinical Trial Registry (ChiCTR2200063161) on 01 Sep 2022 and the first patient was enrolled after pre-registration.

title: Effectiveness of psychosocial interventions addressing informal caregivers' mental health: an umbrella systematic review with 26,481 participants.
authors: Bano B, Cristofalo D, Prina E et al.
abstract:
AIM: We aimed to provide a comprehensive overview of the effectiveness of psychosocial interventions on informal caregivers' mental health, organized by the clinical condition(s) of the care recipient.
METHODS: We conducted an umbrella systematic review and random-effects meta-analyses to pool the results of the included studies for each combination of clinical condition, intervention type, comparison and outcome.
RESULTS: We included 19 systematic reviews and 50 meta-analyses, with 26,481 participants. Several interventions improved mental health outcomes in caregivers, and across various clinical conditions of the care recipients. In dementia caregivers, multicomponent interventions significantly reduced depressive and anxiety symptoms, and caregiver burden (SMD from -0.65 to -0.19). For caregivers of people with lung cancer, psychoeducation and psychological support reduced depressive (SMD = -1.66, 95% CI -3.19 to -0.13) and anxiety symptoms (SMD = -1.37, 95% CI -2.54 to -0.21). Multicomponent interventions reduced depressive and anxiety symptoms in parents of children with cancer (SMD = -0.38, 95% CI -0.64 to -0.12; SMD = -0.89, 95% CI -1.33 to -0.45). Caregiver burden of caregivers of people with psychosis and schizophrenia decreased after psychoeducation and skills-training (SMD = -2.10, 95% CI -3.46 to -0.74; SMD = -0.94, 95% CI -1.72 to -0.17). Certainty of evidence was low to moderate, and the strength of association was overall weak.
CONCLUSIONS: We rigorously assessed the quality, certainty of evidence, and the strength of associations. Despite the appraisals highlighting the need for further high-quality research, our results can inform policy and practice on the use of psychosocial interventions for caregivers of people with different clinical conditions.

title: Machine learning for differentiating primary lung cancer from pulmonary metastases and non-small cell lung cancer histological subtype classification: a systematic review.
authors: Zare O, Ostovari M, Mahmoudi T
abstract:
AIM: This study aimed to systematically review machine learning (ML) methods applied to computed tomography (CT) and positron emission tomography (PET)/CT for differentiating primary lung cancer from pulmonary metastases and for lung cancer histological subtype classification.
MATERIALS AND METHODS: PubMed/MEDLINE, Web of Science, and IEEE Xplore were searched for original peer-reviewed studies published from January 2010 to May 31, 2026. Eligible studies applied ML, deep learning, or radiomics to CT, PET, or PET/CT for primary versus metastatic lung lesion differentiation or major lung cancer histological subtype classification. Methodological quality was assessed with Quality assessment of comparative diagnostic accuracy studies (QUADAS-2), and reporting was evaluated using 10 prespecified Checklist for Artificial Intelligence in Medical Imaging-aligned items.
RESULTS: Twenty-two studies were included after eligibility reassessment. Twenty-one provided a numeric study-level Area Under the Curve (AUC); the median representative AUC was 0.889 (IQR 0.820-0.936). The median AUC was 0.923 for primary/metastatic differentiation and 0.874 for histological subtype classification. Only 5 of 22 studies (22.7%) used independent external testing; among 4 externally validated studies with numeric AUCs, the median was 0.720. QUADAS-2 showed frequent uncertainty in patient selection (17/22, 77.3%), while CLAIM-aligned assessment identified limited external testing, code/model availability (3/22, 13.6%), and explainability reporting (4/22, 18.2%).
CONCLUSION: CT- and PET/CT-based ML models show promising diagnostic performance for lung lesion-origin and histological subtype classification, but performance is lower in independent external evaluation. Broader multicentre validation, transparent reporting, reproducible code/model access, and prospective assessment are required before routine clinical implementation.

title: Skeletal muscle depletion during neoadjuvant chemoimmunotherapy predicts postoperative complications in non-small cell lung cancer: a retrospective cohort study.
authors: Feng W, Wang X, Du H et al.
abstract:
BACKGROUND: For patients with resectable locally advanced non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC), surgical resection preceded by neoadjuvant chemoimmunotherapy (nICT) has become the standard treatment strategy. However, the triple physiological burden imposed by chemotherapy, immunotherapy, and ongoing tumor metabolism may compromise functional reserve and increase surgical risk. Identifying patients at high risk for postoperative complications remains a critical challenge in perioperative management. This study aimed to characterize dynamic changes in skeletal muscle and adipose tissue during nICT, to identify independent predictors of postoperative complications, and to evaluate the incremental predictive value of dynamic body composition metrics over established clinical variables.
METHODS: This retrospective study included 160 patients with resectable NSCLC who underwent surgical resection following nICT between June 2024 and December 2025. Skeletal muscle index (SMI), skeletal muscle density (SMD), visceral adipose tissue (VAT), and subcutaneous adipose tissue (SAT) were quantified at the L3 vertebral level on computed tomography (CT) images obtained before and after treatment. Dynamic changes (Δ) were calculated as the difference between pre-treatment and post-treatment values. The primary outcome was postoperative complications of Clavien-Dindo (CD) grade ≥II. Three predictive models were constructed and compared using area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUC), net reclassification improvement (NRI), and integrated discrimination improvement (IDI).
RESULTS: Following nICT, skeletal muscle metrics decreased significantly (median ΔSMI, -0.54 cm2/m2; P=0.01; median ΔSMD, -0.90 HU; P=0.003), while adipose tissue areas increased significantly (median ΔVAT, 9.54 cm2; P<0.001; median ΔSAT, 8.06 cm2; P<0.001). No significant correlation was observed between ΔSMI and ΔVAT (Spearman ρ=0.087; P=0.27), indicating divergent and independent metabolic trajectories. Of 160 patients, 58 (36.3%) developed CD grade ≥ II complications. Among the four dynamic body-composition measures, each evaluated in a separate multivariable model, only ΔSMI remained significantly associated with postoperative complications [adjusted odds ratio (OR) =0.806; 95% confidence interval (CI): 0.721-0.900; P<0.001], whereas ΔSMD, ΔVAT, and ΔSAT did not. Traditional assessments, including body mass index (BMI) change, Eastern Cooperative Oncology Group (ECOG) performance status, pulmonary function, and systemic inflammatory and nutritional indices, likewise showed no significant associations. Adding ΔSMI to the clinical model significantly improved AUC from 0.595 to 0.710 (ΔAUC =0.115; P=0.007).
CONCLUSIONS: Dynamic loss of skeletal muscle during nICT, as assessed on routine CT images, was independently associated with postoperative complications in patients with resectable NSCLC. Compared with baseline body-composition parameters and conventional clinical indices, longitudinal change in SMI (ΔSMI) provided better discrimination of perioperative risk. Because ΔSMI can be derived from CT scans already obtained for treatment-response assessment, it may serve as a practical, low-burden imaging biomarker to support preoperative risk stratification and identify patients who may benefit from targeted prehabilitation.

title: Pretreatment prediction of early severe treatment-related toxicity in older patients with lung adenocarcinoma: same-center temporal validation of a risk model.
authors: Sun H, Chen X, Feng J et al.
abstract:
BACKGROUND: Older adults with lung adenocarcinoma have heterogeneous tolerance of chemotherapy-based treatment. Early severe toxicity can disrupt planned therapy, require unplanned admission, and limit treatment intensity. We developed a pretreatment risk model for severe treatment-related toxicity within the first two chemotherapy-based cycles and examined whether Fatigue, Resistance, Ambulation, Illnesses, and Loss of weight (FRAIL) category and inflammatory-nutritional markers add risk-stratification information.
METHODS: This single-center retrospective cohort included patients aged ≥60 years with pathologically confirmed lung adenocarcinoma who received cytotoxic chemotherapy-based systemic treatment between September 2015 and September 2025. Among 1,106 screened patients, 1,019 formed the primary complete-case cohort; a multiple-imputation sensitivity analysis included 1,045 patients with eligible treatment exposure and adjudicable outcomes. Patients treated from September 2015 to December 2021 formed the development cohort (n=679), and those treated from January 2022 to September 2025 formed the same-center temporal validation cohort (n=340). The endpoint was Common Terminology Criteria for Adverse Events (CTCAE) version 5.0 grade ≥3 treatment-related toxicity within the first two cycles. Model A contained clinical variables, Model B added FRAIL category, and Model C additionally incorporated the neutrophil-to-lymphocyte ratio (NLR) and prognostic nutritional index (PNI). Performance was assessed using discrimination, calibration, Brier score, decision curve analysis, and risk grouping.
RESULTS: Severe treatment-related toxicity occurred in 316 of 1,019 patients (31.0%): 202 in the development cohort and 114 in the validation cohort. Toxicity rates increased across FRAIL categories: 13.5% in robust, 28.5% in pre-frail, and 51.4% in frail patients (P for trend <0.001). In Model C, frailty, higher Eastern Cooperative Oncology Group (ECOG) performance status, tumor-node-metastasis (TNM) stage IV disease, and lower PNI indicated greater risk. Model C yielded an area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUC) of 0.770 [95% confidence interval (CI): 0.736-0.809] in development and 0.753 (95% CI: 0.700-0.805) in validation. In the validation cohort, the calibration intercept was 0.124 (95% CI: -0.194 to 0.442) and slope was 0.986 (95% CI: 0.706-1.267). Model C also produced ordered low-, intermediate-, and high-risk strata with increasing observed toxicity rates.
CONCLUSIONS: A pretreatment model combining clinical variables, FRAIL category, NLR, and PNI separated older patients with lung adenocarcinoma into different levels of early severe toxicity risk. The model showed moderate discrimination, acceptable calibration, and directionally consistent sensitivity analyses. It may support closer observation and supportive-care planning, but routine use should await multicenter external validation and prospective evaluation of clinical impact.

title: Where Eastern Medicine Meets Western Medicine: A World Review of the Management of Chronic Cough.
authors: Teng TZJ, Koh ZX, Lim JYS et al.
journal: World J Otorhinolaryngol Head Neck Surg
abstract:
PURPOSE: To summarize current Western and Eastern approaches to the evaluation and management of chronic cough, with particular emphasis on etiology-directed therapy, cough hypersensitivity, behavioral interventions, neuromodulators, procedural treatments, and traditional remedies.
METHODS: A literature search of PubMed, Web of Science, CNKI, and Ovid Medline was conducted on February 1, 2024. Adults with chronic cough lasting at least 8 weeks were eligible. Pediatric studies, studies involving immunocompromised patients, smokers or patients with lung cancer, animal studies, and non-English or non-Mandarin publications were excluded. Because of substantial heterogeneity in etiologies, interventions, study designs, and outcome measures, findings were synthesized narratively rather than quantitatively. Twenty-three primary studies were included in the final narrative synthesis.
RESULTS: Chronic cough commonly reflects cough hypersensitivity involving vagal sensory pathways and receptors including TRPV1, TRPA1, and P2X3. Common clinical contributors included upper airway cough syndrome, gastro-esophageal reflux disease, and cough-variant asthma. Management was most appropriately organized as a stepwise approach involving identification and treatment of the underlying cause, behavioral cough suppression therapy, and selected pharmacological treatment. Gabapentin and P2X3 antagonists may benefit refractory cough, although adverse effects and limited long-term data remain important limitations. Superior laryngeal nerve block and antireflux surgery may be considered in carefully selected patients. Acupuncture and selected traditional preparations may provide adjunctive benefit, but the evidence remains heterogeneous and should not replace standard evaluation or treatment.
CONCLUSION: Chronic cough should be managed using a personalized, stepwise strategy that combines etiology-directed treatment with interventions targeting cough hypersensitivity. Traditional therapies may have a complementary role, but further well-designed comparative studies are required.
