title: Claudin 18.2: From a Tight Junction Protein to a Breakthrough Target in Solid Tumor Immunotherapy.
authors: Bahrami M, Makoui MH, Bayat Bodaghi A et al.
abstract: Claudin 18.2 (CLDN18.2), a tight junction protein largely confined to normal gastric mucosa, is overexpressed and mislocalized on the surface of gastric, gastroesophageal, pancreatic, and other gastrointestinal cancers. This pattern has made CLDN18.2 a leading target in solid tumor immunotherapy. This review traces its path from a structural junctional component to a clinically relevant antigen and assesses the therapeutic platforms built around it. We discuss monoclonal antibodies, especially zolbetuximab, whose phase III SPOTLIGHT and GLOW trials improved survival in CLDN18.2-positive, HER2-negative gastric and gastroesophageal junction adenocarcinoma and led to regulatory approval. We then evaluate antibody-drug conjugates, bispecific T-cell engagers, and CAR T-cell therapies, comparing their mechanisms, efficacy, toxicity, and resistance. We also examine the rationale for combining CLDN18.2-directed agents with immune checkpoint inhibitors, although clinical evidence for synergy remains indirect. Major challenges include antigen loss and heterogeneity, autophagy-mediated ADC resistance, on-target gastrointestinal toxicity, cytokine release syndrome, and unstandardized expression thresholds. Because optimal cutoffs differ by modality, patient selection should follow the intended therapeutic class rather than a universal biomarker score. Overall, CLDN18.2-directed therapy is a maturing precision oncology strategy; its impact will depend on randomized data, better biomarkers, and rational combinations.

title: Recent advances in targeted therapies and immunotherapies for triple-negative breast cancer.
authors: Rashid G, Elsori D, Naqvi Z et al.
abstract: This comprehensive review explores advancements in the treatment of Triple-Negative Breast Cancer (TNBC), emphasizing the transformative impact of targeted therapies and immunotherapies. Given TNBC's aggressive nature and limited therapeutic options, this review provides an in-depth analysis of emerging strategies that aim to enhance patient outcomes. Within targeted therapies, we discuss molecular subtypes and evaluate the efficacy of PARP inhibitors, EGFR inhibitors, and PI3K inhibitors, integrating insights from clinical trials. The immunotherapy landscape is examined through immune checkpoint inhibitors, Chimeric Antigen Receptor (CAR) T-cell therapy, and novel vaccine-based approaches. Combination strategies are assessed, focusing on clinical efficacy, safety, and resistance mechanisms. Additionally, we highlight emerging therapeutic innovations, including bispecific antibodies, advanced drug delivery systems, and personalized medicine approaches. Beyond treatment modalities, the review addresses key challenges such as therapy resistance, biomarker-driven treatment selection, and the integration of Artificial Intelligence in TNBC management. Future directions emphasize ongoing clinical trials and evolving therapeutic paradigms aimed at improving survival and quality of life for TNBC patients. As the field progresses, a multidisciplinary approach integrating precision oncology, innovative therapeutics, and patient-centered care will be critical. In conclusion, this review encapsulates current breakthroughs and envisions a future where targeted and immune-based interventions redefine TNBC treatment, offering new hope for patients and clinicians alike.

title: B7-H3-mediated immune regulation in cancer: biological functions and therapeutic opportunities.
authors: Shreshtha S, Kaluarachchige L, Meyer OA et al.
abstract: B7-H3 (CD276), a member of the B7 family of immunoregulatory ligands, has emerged as an important molecule at the intersection of tumor biology and cancer immunology. Although initially identified as a regulator of T-cell responses, accumulating evidence supports its predominantly immunosuppressive role. B7-H3 is highly expressed across diverse malignancies, including brain, prostate, lung, breast, colorectal, and pediatric cancers, while showing limited expression in most normal adult tissues. Its tumor-associated expression, including tumor vasculature, makes B7-H3 an attractive therapeutic target. Beyond immune regulation, B7-H3 promotes tumor progression through tumor cell-intrinsic mechanisms involving PI3K/AKT, NF-κB, and STAT3 signaling, angiogenesis, epithelial-to-mesenchymal plasticity, and metabolic reprogramming. Within the tumor microenvironment, B7-H3 suppresses T-cell and natural killer cell activity and promotes immunosuppressive macrophage polarization, while its expression can be regulated by metabolic and epigenetic mechanisms. These multifaceted functions have stimulated the development of diverse B7-H3-targeted therapies, including monoclonal antibodies, antibody-drug conjugates, CAR T-cell and Vδ1 T-cell therapies, nanobody-based platforms, and bispecific or trispecific immune cell engagers. Early clinical studies have demonstrated promising antitumor activity, although important challenges regarding efficacy, safety, tumor heterogeneity, and patient selection remain. In this review, we summarize the molecular regulation and biological functions of B7-H3, critically evaluate the current development of B7-H3-targeted therapies, and discuss key challenges and future directions for translating B7-H3-directed strategies into effective cancer treatments.

title: Clinical trial landscape and translational priorities for adoptive T-cell and NK-cell therapies in gynecologic malignancies.
authors: Chen Q, Zhu Y, Ye S et al.
abstract:
BACKGROUND: Adoptive T-cell and natural killer (NK)-cell therapies are expanding across solid tumors, but their registered development in gynecologic malignancies remains difficult to interpret because many studies use basket designs and registry records vary in detail.
METHODS: We conducted a cross-sectional analysis of therapeutic adoptive T-cell and NK-cell trial records identified from TrialTrove, ClinicalTrials.gov, and the WHO International Clinical Trials Registry Platform. Trials were classified into three mutually exclusive evidence-specificity groups: single gynecologic disease family specific, multiple gynecologic disease families only, and broader baskets including non-gynecologic cancers. We evaluated source sensitivity, target applicability, field-specific registry visibility, and the availability of posted registry safety results. A complementary registry-informed exploratory survey of 25 experts assessed translational barriers and development priorities using domain-specific 1-5 scales.
RESULTS: Among 442 unique records screened, 211 therapeutic trials met the eligibility criteria. Of these, 43 were restricted to a single gynecologic disease family, 2 included multiple gynecologic disease families only, and 166 were broader basket trials permitting enrollment of non-gynecologic malignancies. The public-registry-linked and public-search-captured sensitivity subsets included 200 and 141 records, respectively, with broadly similar structural patterns across datasets. The landscape was predominantly early phase, with 149 Phase I and 50 Phase I/II trials. CAR-T, TIL, and TCR-T were the leading modalities, accounting for 79, 60, and 42 trials, respectively. Only 20 records had posted registry results with an adverse-event module, indicating limited availability of registry-reported safety data. In the exploratory expert survey, an immunosuppressive tumor microenvironment and a lack of gynecologic-specific cohorts were identified as leading barriers, whereas ovarian cancer, TIL therapy, MSLN, target reporting, and registry completeness emerged as prominent development priorities.
CONCLUSIONS: Registered cellular-therapy activity in gynecologic malignancies is broad but remains early phase, largely basket-derived, and unevenly visible in registry fields. Separating disease-specific trials from broader eligibility-only baskets, testing source sensitivity, and distinguishing modality biology from missing target reporting provide a more reproducible basis for future trial planning.

title: Rewiring the Tumor-Immune Ecosystem: Extracellular Vesicles in the Next Era of Cancer Immunotherapy.
authors: Bahr AR, Basem Y, Alaa A et al.
abstract: Cancer immunotherapy has transformed oncology by enabling immune-mediated tumor elimination; however, durable responses remain limited, particularly in solid tumors due to antigen heterogeneity, immunosuppressive tumor microenvironment, and adaptive resistance mechanisms. To overcome these barriers, therapeutic paradigms are expanding from single-agent interventions toward programmable cellular and acellular platforms. This review examines recent advances in CAR-T, CAR-NK, and TCR-engineered cell therapies alongside key resistance mechanisms. In parallel, we evaluate the dual biological role of extracellular vesicles (EVs) as mediators of immune evasion and as engineered delivery tools. Rather than presenting multimodal integration as an inherently superior solution, we critically evaluate the trade-offs of combining engineered cells, EVs, checkpoint blockade, oncolytic viruses, and targeted agents, focusing on therapeutic synergy versus cumulative toxicity and biomanufacturing complexity. Collectively, we propose that future cancer immunotherapy will rely on multi-modal, adaptive, and systems-level engineering approaches capable of dynamically reshaping the tumor-immune ecosystem to achieve sustained tumor regression and durable overall survival.

title: Toward the next generation of CAR T cell therapies for cancer.
authors: Usta D, Mackall CL
abstract: With seven products approved by the US Food and Drug Administration (FDA) for 15 indications and more than 2,600 active clinical trials, chimeric antigen receptor (CAR) T cell therapy is firmly established as an effective therapeutic modality for cancer treatment, and promising early data demonstrate its potential in autoimmune diseases. Key challenges facing the field include extending efficacy to solid tumors and reducing the cost and complexity of manufacturing to improve patient access. In this review, we summarize the clinical lessons learned from the now substantial experience with commercial CAR T cells and clinical trials and discuss three waves shaping next-generation development: multi-engineered and logic-gated CAR T cells, rational combination strategies, and in vivo CAR T cell generation. By integrating clinical experience with emerging strategies, we highlight where CAR T cell therapy has succeeded, where current approaches remain insufficient, and how next-generation cell therapies may be designed to overcome these barriers.

title: MRI Biomarkers for Brain Metastases in Lung Cancer Using Machine Learning
summary: Purpose: Existing prognostic models for brain metastases from lung cancer rely on clinical variables and do not capture the biological heterogeneity of host or tumor factors underlying survival outcomes. We evaluated whether MRI-derived radiomic biomarkers improve prognostic stratification beyond clinical variables. We also investigated their biological correlates using matched histopathology. Experimental Design: This retrospective study included 103 patients with brain metastases from lung cancer and matched pre-operative MRI and histopathology. Radiomic features from T1-weighted contrast-enhanced and T2-weighted fluid-attenuated inversion recovery sequences were combined with clinical variables to train Cox proportional hazards, random survival forest, and DeepSurv models for overall survival (OS), CNS progression, and leptomeningeal (LM) progression. Risk groups from an imaging-only model were compared for clinical and histopathologic differences. Results: Imaging features improved prognostic performance beyond clinical variables across all modeling frameworks, with the combined clinical-imaging DeepSurv model achieving the highest concordance index for OS (0.728). Risk groups from the best-performing model for each endpoint differed significantly in OS (median 26.7 vs. 9.1 months, p < 0.001) and LM progression (p = 0.003), but not in CNS progression. Imaging-only risk groups did not differ significantly in any clinical variable, but high-risk patients were less likely to have tumor-infiltrating lymphocytes (46% vs. 77%, p = 0.010) and PD-L1 expression [≥] 50% (10% vs. 32%, p = 0.049). Conclusions: MRI radiomic biomarkers provide prognostic information beyond established clinical variables in lung cancer brain metastases and correspond to features of the tumor immune microenvironment, supporting their potential to refine risk stratification.

title: Catabolism of extracellular glutathione is a driver of metastasis formation
summary: Metastasizing cancer cells require metabolic plasticity to adapt to the microenvironment of the target organ. Analyzing metabolites in interstitial fluids, we found that the liver microenvironment is devoid of cystine but contains high concentrations of glutathione (GSH). Detailed mechanistic analysis revealed that cancer cells degrade extracellular GSH utilizing gamma-glutamyl-transferase (GGT) activity for provision of cysteine to support proliferation and prevent ferroptosis under cystine-free conditions. This was independent of system Xc- but required activity of glutamate-cysteine ligase (GCLC). GGT1 expression was associated with poor survival and upregulated in liver metastases of human breast cancer patients. Overexpression of Ggt1 in murine breast cancer cells enhanced their capacity for liver colonization and promoted lung metastases after orthotopic implantation. This identifies extracellular GSH catabolism as driver of metastasis that supports proliferation and oxidative stress resistance in metabolically challenging microenvironments.

title: PIEZO1 marks a low neuroendocrine state and supports cisplatin tolerance in small cell lung cancer
summary: Small cell lung cancer (SCLC) is initially sensitive to platinum chemotherapy, yet resistant disease frequently develops with altered neuroendocrine (NE) identity. The mechanisms linking these cell states to treatment tolerance remain incompletely understood. Here, we integrate chemoresistant cell models with patient bulk multiomics, single-cell and spatial transcriptomic data to investigate the mechanosensitive channel PIEZO1. In H69AR cells, PIEZO1 upregulation accompanied loss of NE markers and enrichment of mesenchymal programmes; increased PIEZO1 expression and reduced cisplatin sensitivity were also observed in H446DDP cells. Across patient-derived data sources, PIEZO1 was associated with low NE activity within malignant populations, despite its substantially higher abundance in vascular and stromal cells. State-blind CNV analyses and cross-sectional state ordering supported a cell-state association that was only weakly explained by detectable subclones and varied with hypoxia across models. Spatial analyses localized PIEZO1-rich signals to stromal and vascular interface regions, while composition-adjusted tumour-core analyses showed little residual covariance with tumour programmes. PIEZO1 depletion reduced intracellular calcium-associated signals and cisplatin IC50 and increased drug-induced apoptosis. Conversely, Yoda1 increased calcium signals and cisplatin tolerance in parental cells. Patient light-chain phosphorylation, YAP localization and partial pharmacological reversal by verteporfin supported an actomyosin-YAP-linked mechanism. PIEZO1 depletion also reduced SMAD2/3 and mesenchymal-associated readouts. Finally, transcript enrichment profiles and PIEZO1-IGF2BP2 covariation nominated a potential m6A regulatory layer. Together, these findings identify PIEZO1 as a low-NE state-associated marker and contributor to cisplatin tolerance, and motivate a calcium-cytoskeleton-YAP model for further mechanistic testing.

title: Jideytro (zidesamtinib) for previously treated ros1-positive non-small cell lung cancer: a new era in post-tki therapy.
authors: Zahra Hujjat SF, Islam MT
abstract: ROS1-positive non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC) is a distinct oncogene-driven subtype that commonly affects younger, never-smokers and frequently develops central nervous system metastases and kinase-domain resistance mutations. Although first- and second-generation ROS1 tyrosine kinase inhibitors (TKIs) have improved outcomes, most patients eventually progress after treatment. On 22 July 2026, the U.S. Food and Drug Administration approved Jideytro (zidesamtinib) for adults with locally advanced or metastatic ROS1-positive NSCLC previously treated with a ROS1 TKI. Zidesamtinib is a selective, brain-penetrant, macrocyclic ROS1 inhibitor that spares tropomyosin receptor kinase (TRK) signaling while maintaining activity against diverse resistance mutations, including G2032R. In the pivotal ARROS-1 trial, it produced durable responses in heavily pretreated patients, including those with brain metastases, with low treatment discontinuation. Although prospective comparisons with crizotinib, entrectinib, repotrectinib, and taletrectinib are needed, zidesamtinib represents an important addition to post-TKI therapy for ROS1-positive NSCLC.

title: Zidesamtinib in ROS1-positive NSCLC with brain metastases: clinical evidence and therapeutic implications.
authors: Sheikh A, Saleem S, Imran SB et al.

title: Bioactive compounds from Perilla frutescens modulate multiple cell death pathways and signaling networks in cancer therapy.
authors: Xu H, Liu J, Wu H et al.
abstract: Perilla frutescens, an edible medicinal plant from East Asia, produces diverse bioactive phytochemicals with anticancer activity, including perillaldehyde (PAH), rosmarinic acid (RA), luteolin, apigenin, and alpha-linolenic acid (ALA). These compounds exert multi-target anticancer effects through apoptosis, autophagy, and ferroptosis. PAH triggers ferroptosis in gastric cancer via the System Xc-/GSH/GPX4 axis and P62-Keap1-Nrf2 pathway, while inducing protective autophagy in colorectal cancer through SRD5A1 and PI3K/AKT modulation. RA directly binds KRAS(G12C) and suppresses NSCLC via KRAS/AKT/ERK, and inhibits stress-induced TNBC metastasis through Src inactivation. Perilla leaf extracts activate Hippo-YAP/TAZ signaling in breast cancer. ALA-rich perilla seed oil (PSO) mitigates tumorigenesis in colitis-associated colorectal cancer models and restores gut microbial homeostasis. This review synthesizes current molecular evidence on perilla compounds in cancer therapy, focusing on apoptosis-autophagy-ferroptosis crosstalk. The multi-target characteristics position perilla-derived compounds as adjuvant cancer therapy candidates, though bioavailability and clinical translation still challenges remain.

title: Efficacy and safety of neoadjuvant targeted therapy in surgically treated patients with ALK-rearranged non-small cell lung cancer.
authors: Liu Y, Fang L, Jiang Z et al.
abstract:
BACKGROUND: Anaplastic lymphoma kinase (ALK) tyrosine kinase inhibitors (TKIs) have demonstrated substantial efficacy in advanced ALK-rearranged non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC), but evidence for their use in the neoadjuvant setting remains limited. This study aimed to evaluate and compare the efficacy and safety of neoadjuvant ALK-targeted therapy and chemotherapy-based neoadjuvant treatment in surgically treated patients with ALK-rearranged NSCLC.
METHODS: We retrospectively analyzed the clinical data of 20 patients with ALK-rearranged NSCLC who received neoadjuvant therapy followed by curative-intent surgery at the Department of Thoracic Surgery, Hunan Cancer Hospital, between October 2018 and April 2025. Patients were retrospectively classified into an ALK-TKI group (n=13) and a chemotherapy-based group (n=7) according to the neoadjuvant regimen received. A comparative analysis assessed radiological response, pathological response, postoperative complications, adverse events, and survival outcomes between the 2 groups after neoadjuvant therapy.
RESULTS: The baseline characteristics of the 2 groups were comparable without statistically significant differences. Among the 13 patients in the ALK-TKI group, 9 achieved partial response (PR) and 4 had stable disease (SD), resulting in an objective response rate (ORR) of 69.2%. Among the 7 patients in the chemotherapy-based group, 3 achieved PR and 4 had SD, resulting in an ORR of 42.9% (P=0.35). Six patients (46.2%) in the ALK-TKI group and one patient (14.3%) in the chemotherapy-based group achieved major pathological response (MPR) (P=0.32). Four patients (30.8%) in the ALK-TKI group and one patient (14.3%) in the chemotherapy-based group achieved pathological complete response (pCR) (P=0.61). The proportion of patients with ypN0 disease was significantly higher in the ALK-TKI group than in the chemotherapy-based group (11/13 vs. 3/7, P=0.043), and the extent of pathological nodal downstaging was also greater in the ALK-TKI group (P=0.008). There were no significant differences between the 2 groups in the incidence of adverse events, grade ≥3 adverse events, postoperative complications, surgical approach, operative time, blood loss, thoracic drainage duration, or postoperative hospital stay. Kaplan-Meier analyses showed nonsignificant numerical trends toward improved overall survival and recurrence-free survival in the ALK-TKI group. However, these findings were based on a small number of recurrence and death events and should be interpreted with caution.
CONCLUSIONS: Neoadjuvant ALK-TKI therapy showed numerically higher radiological and pathological response rates and a significantly higher ypN0 rate and greater pathological nodal downstaging relative to the baseline clinical nodal stage compared with chemotherapy-based neoadjuvant therapy. No statistically significant differences in the observed safety or perioperative outcomes were identified between the groups.

title: Evaluating immunocytochemistry performance in lung cancer cytology: An IASLC Cytology Working Group study.
authors: Jain D, Srebotnik-Kirbis I, Nambirajan A et al.
abstract:
BACKGROUND: Immunohistochemistry (IHC) is essential for tumor subtyping and predictive biomarker analysis in non-small cell lung carcinoma (NSCLC). When only cytological material is available and no concurrent biopsy or cell block exists, immunocytochemistry (ICC) may need to be performed on slides prepared using diverse fixation protocols, introducing substantial pre-analytical variability.
METHODS: Seven laboratories representing commonly used cytology fixation protocols were selected based on an exploratory global survey of 63 institutions. Two central laboratories prepared direct smears, cytospins and provided cells in PreservCyt from specimens with confirmed marker expression using the selected fixation protocols. Materials were distributed for immunocytochemical demonstration of TTF-1, p40, ALK, and ROS1 according to local protocols. Digitized slides were independently evaluated using standardized four-tier scoring criteria.
RESULT: A total of 105 stained slides from 17 study runs were assessed. Delaunay-fixed, Papanicolaou-stained, and methanol-fixed polyethylene glycol-coated preparations demonstrated consistently superior ICC performance compared with other evaluated fixation protocols. In contrast, high rates of suboptimal staining were observed with PreservCyt fixation (81.8%) and air-dried preparations (58.8%).
CONCLUSIONS: This study demonstrates that fixation protocol significantly impacts ICC performance on non-cell block cytological preparations. The observed fixation-dependent differences underscore the need for harmonized pre-analytical practices, robust local validation, and external quality assessment.

title: Benzisothiazole derivatives as KRAS G12C inhibitors for potential treatment of non-small cell lung cancer.
authors: Cheng L, Hou SJ, Nie Q et al.
abstract: KRAS G12C mutation is a key driver of multiple solid tumors, and has recently become a crucial target for therapy via small molecules that covalently bind to the mutated cysteine. Herein, a series of benzisothiazole derivatives is presented as KRAS G12C inhibitors utilizing a scaffold-hopping strategy. Among them, S32 exhibited remarkable antiproliferative efficacy, specifically in the NCI-H23 cell line (IC50 = 0.55 ± 0.05 μM). Docking studies of S32 revealed that the oxygen atom of the trifluoroethoxy group at the C-7 position of benzisothiazole formed a hydrogen bond with His95 and extended into a solvent-exposed region. Additionally, S32 obviously inhibited nucleotide exchange efficiency, stabilizing KRAS in the GDP-bound state and inhibited the downstream ERK/AKT signaling pathways of KRAS in NCI-H23 and NCI-H358 cells, while inducing apoptosis by upregulating BAX and downregulating BCL-2 apoptotic proteins. Furthermore, S32 achieved a tumor growth inhibition (TGI) of 90.8% at a dose of 30 mg/kg. These results confirmed that S32, with a benzisothiazole scaffold, was an effective KRAS G12C inhibitor, potentially promoting cancer therapy development.

title: Neoadjuvant Iruplinalkib and Bevacizumab in ALK-positive NSCLC: A Phase II Single-arm Trial
interventions: Bevacizumab combined with iruplinalkib as neoadjuvant therapy in ALK-positive NSCLC:
summary: This is a single-center, single-arm, prospective phase II trial evaluating iruplinalkib plus bevacizumab as neoadjuvant therapy in ALK-positive NSCLC. Eligible patients receive 4 cycles (Q3W) of iruplinalkib (60 mg lead-in for 7 days, then 180 mg daily, PO) plus bevacizumab (15 mg/kg, IV, D1). Surgery is performed 4 weeks later, followed by adjuvant iruplinalkib monotherapy for up to 2 years. Primary endpoint is major pathological response (MPR) rate; secondary endpoints include safety, R0 resection rate, and survival outcomes.

title: MRI-Based 2.5D Multi-Instance Deep Learning for Differentiating Pathological Subtypes of Brain Metastases From Lung Cancer.
authors: Zhu J, Liu C, Zou L et al.
abstract:
BACKGROUND: Distinct treatment strategies for small-cell lung cancer (SCLC) and non-small-cell lung cancer (NSCLC) brain metastases require accurate noninvasive subtyping.
PURPOSE: To develop and externally validate a biparametric MRI-based 2.5D multi-instance learning (MIL) deep learning (DL) model for discriminating SCLC from NSCLC brain metastases, with performance compared against clinical, radiomics, and 3D-DL models.
STUDY TYPE: Retrospective.
POPULATION: This study included 366 patients from four institutions. Center 1 provided the training set (n = 199; mean age, 63.88 ± 10.79 years; 72.36% male) and an internal tuning set (n = 85; mean age, 64.73 ± 9.53 years; 67.06% male). Centers 2-4 were pooled into a single external test set (n = 82; mean age, 62.26 ± 10.60 years; 63.41% male).
FIELD STRENGTH/SEQUENCE: 1.5 T and 3.0 T; contrast-enhanced T1-weighted imaging and fluid-attenuated inversion-recovery imaging.
ASSESSMENT: The 2.5D-MIL model was benchmarked against clinical, radiomics, and 3D-DL models and evaluated on internal tuning and pooled external test sets.
STATISTICAL TESTS: Shapiro-Wilk, Student's t-test, Mann-Whitney U, chi-square, univariable and multivariable logistic regression, and DeLong tests were used. Performance measures included the area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUC) with 95% confidence intervals and classification and calibration metrics. Statistical significance was defined as two-sided p < 0.05.
RESULTS: In the internal tuning set, AUCs were 0.842 (2.5D-MIL), 0.740 (clinical), 0.710 (radiomics), and 0.747 (3D-DL). In the external test set, AUCs were 0.826 (2.5D-MIL), 0.826 (clinical), 0.696 (radiomics), and 0.664 (3D-DL). Differences between 2.5D-MIL and the clinical (p = 1.000), radiomics (p = 0.139), and 3D-DL (p = 0.119) models were not significant.
DATA CONCLUSION: The MRI-based 2.5D-MIL model showed potential for noninvasive differentiation of SCLC from NSCLC brain metastases. Larger prospective studies are needed before clinical use.
EVIDENCE LEVEL: 3.
TECHNICAL EFFICACY: Stage 2.

title: Spontaneous regression of a combined large cell neuroendocrine carcinoma following bronchoscopic biopsy: A case of cytohistological discordance.
authors: Kawamura T, Kawabata S, Oishi T et al.
abstract: Spontaneous regression (SR) in lung cancer is extremely rare. We report a unique case of apparent biopsy-associated SR accompanied by cytohistological diagnostic discordance in a 68-year-old man. The patient presented with a 14-mm pulmonary nodule. Bronchoscopic forceps biopsy initially yielded a diagnosis of small cell lung cancer (SCLC), whereas concurrent brush cytology suggested non-small cell lung cancer. Unexpectedly, a preoperative computed tomography scan obtained 41 days after biopsy revealed regression of the solid tumour component from 14 mm to 7 mm. The patient underwent surgical resection, and the final pathological evaluation revealed combined lung cancer comprising predominantly adenocarcinoma (95%) with a minor large-cell neuroendocrine carcinoma component (5%). The initial SCLC diagnosis was based on crush artefact within the biopsy specimen, which obscured the characteristic morphology of LCNEC. This case highlights that physical biopsy can trigger transient SR, particularly in neuroendocrine tumours; however, surgical resection remains essential to address heterogeneous disease progression. Furthermore, cytohistological discordance should alert clinicians to the possibility of combined tumours, intratumoural heterogeneity, and morphological pitfalls, ensuring appropriate multidisciplinary management.

title: Does thermal ablation plus chemotherapy improve survival in small-cell lung cancer ineligible for surgery?
authors: Sun M, Zhang Y, Tang Y et al.
abstract:
BACKGROUND: Thermal ablation (TA) is a safe and feasible alternative for the treatment of non-small cell lung cancer. However, data on the clinical efficacy of TA in patients with small-cell lung cancer (SCLC) are scarce. This study aimed to explore the clinical efficacy of TA plus chemotherapy (CHT) in treating SCLC.
METHODS: This is a population-based retrospective cohort study based on the Surveillance, Epidemiology and End Results (SEER) database. We collected data from the SEER database for 51,273 SCLC patients who received CHT from 2000 to 2019. Using propensity score matching (PSM), we balanced covariate differences between two treatment groups: CHT alone and TA plus CHT. Kaplan-Meier survival curves for overall survival (OS) and lung cancer-specific survival (LCSS) were generated. Cox regression analysis was conducted to assess independent prognostic indicators.
RESULTS: After PSM, the TA + CHT group exhibited superior OS and LCSS compared to the CHT-only group. Age subgroup analysis revealed that for patients aged ≥70 years, TA + CHT resulted in improved OS and LCSS compared to CHT alone. For patients <70 years, a survival benefit was observed, but the difference was not statistically significant. Tumor size subgroup analysis showed that for patients with tumor sizes of 0-3 cm, TA + CHT led to superior OS and LCSS compared to CHT alone, while no statistically significant differences were observed in other tumor size subgroups. N stage subgroup analysis indicated that for N0 and N1 patients, TA + CHT had better OS and LCSS compared to CHT alone, with no statistically significant differences in the N2 and N3 subgroups. Multivariable analysis indicated that TA + CHT was an independent favorable prognostic indicator for both OS and LCSS.
CONCLUSIONS: TA + CHT may be a promising treatment option for patients with SCLC, especially those aged ≥70 years with tumor size ≤3 cm, and N0-1 disease.

title: Artificial intelligence and radiomics in small cell lung cancer: a narrative review of imaging and multisource data integration.
authors: Yang Y, Sun J, Liu J et al.
abstract:
BACKGROUND AND OBJECTIVE: Artificial intelligence (AI) and radiomics are increasingly used to analyze imaging and multisource data in small cell lung cancer (SCLC), but the directness and clinical maturity of the available evidence remain uncertain. This narrative review aimed to summarize and critically evaluate SCLC-specific, mixed-cohort, and indirect evidence across diagnostic classification, prognostic prediction, treatment-associated outcomes, and lesion segmentation.
METHODS: A structured literature search was conducted to identify human studies evaluating AI, deep learning (DL), radiomics, or machine learning within imaging-based or imaging-integrated workflows. Studies were selected according to clinical relevance, directness of SCLC evidence, methodological strength, and reporting completeness, and were classified as SCLC-specific, mixed-cohort, or indirect/transferable evidence.
KEY CONTENT AND FINDINGS: Direct SCLC-specific evidence was strongest for multicenter computed tomography (CT)-based prognostic models and lesion segmentation, whereas diagnostic classification relied mainly on mixed cohorts or public image-level datasets. Treatment-response models showed preliminary value but were predominantly retrospective and lacked prospective clinical validation. Retrospective studies suggested associations between model-derived risk scores and outcomes following prophylactic cranial irradiation (PCI), but did not establish treatment-benefit prediction. Pathomic and radiogenomic analyses also identified associations between quantitative features, immune-cell infiltration, genomic alterations, and treatment response; these findings remain hypothesis-generating. Interpretation is limited by small SCLC cohorts, retrospective single-center designs, non-independent image-level analyses, and limited external validation and interpretability.
CONCLUSIONS: AI and radiomics show potential in SCLC, particularly for CT-based prognosis and segmentation. However, treatment-response prediction, non-invasive subtype classification, and clinical decision support remain investigational and require prospective multicenter validation and patient-level external evaluation before clinical implementation.

title: Two cases of large cell neuroendocrine carcinoma of the gallbladder: case reports and systemic literature review.
authors: Yang Y, Zhang C, Liu Q et al.
abstract: As gallbladder large cell neuroendocrine carcinoma (GB-LCNEC) is extremely rare and highly aggressive, with limited reports in both domestic and international literature, we herein report two cases of GB-LCNEC accompanied by contiguous high-grade intraepithelial neoplasia of the overlying mucosa. One of the patients had pancreaticobiliary maljunction. Microscopically, the tumor cells were large and arranged in organoid, nested, palisading or trabecular patterns. They exhibited abundant cytoplasm, vesicular nuclei with coarse granular chromatin, prominent nucleoli, and mitotic figures exceeding 20 per 2 mm2. Immunohistochemically, both tumors showed diffuse positivity for the neuroendocrine markers chromogranin A (CgA) and synaptophysin (Syn), and both exhibited a Ki-67 proliferative index exceeding 20%. They demonstrated wild-type and aberrant (mutant) p53 expression patterns, respectively. Although the 2 cases reported in this study were confirmed to have space-occupying lesions in the gallbladder via CT/MRI, preoperative diagnosis was not achieved due to insufficient understanding of the disease. Through a systematic literature review, this study delineates the clinicopathologic and molecular features, diagnostic criteria, differential diagnoses, treatment, and prognosis of GB-LCNEC, as well as its potential pathogenesis/origin that may involve a multistep carcinogenic process of chronic inflammation-metaplasia-dysplasia-carcinogenesis. It aims to enhance clinical understanding of this rare disease and lay the foundation for future related research.

title: A zinc organic metal skeleton vaccine for lung cancer treatment can stimulate strong innate and adaptive anti-tumor immunity.
authors: Liu X, Zhang X, Wang Y et al.
abstract:
BACKGROUND: Tumor-associated macrophages (TAMs) function as central regulators bridging innate and adaptive immunity in the tumor microenvironment (TME). Therapeutic targeting of TAMs to promote M1 polarization represents a critical strategy for tumor suppression.
METHODS: Herein, we engineered a zinc metal-organic framework functionalized with mannose (MAN) and loaded with CLDN6 antigen (Zn-MAN@CLDN6). We systematically evaluated the anti-tumor efficacy and immunomodulatory functions of Zn-MAN@CLDN6 both in vitro and in vivo. The nanoplatform exhibited the potent cytotoxicity against lung cancer cells and enhanced the macrophage-mediated phagocytosis, while promoting M1 polarization and antigen presentation to activate T cells. Mechanistically, single-cell RNA sequencing (scRNA-seq) of tumor tissues elucidated the regulatory networks underlying its macrophage-targeted effects.
RESULTS: The vaccine targeted the highly expressed CD206 receptor on the surface of macrophages through surface modified mannose (MAN), achieving the selective endocytosis. Its acid responsive framework can rapidly degrade under acidic conditions of macrophage lysosomes, releasing Zn2+ ions and the CLDN6 antigen. The released Zn2+ acted as an endogenous adjuvant, driving macrophages towards M1 phenotype polarization and enhancing their antigen presentation ability (manifested as upregulation of CD86, MHC-I/II, and IL-12 expression). Meanwhile, macrophages that had undergone the re-education can present CLDN6 antigen to CD8+ T cells through a cross presentation mechanism, effectively activating specific cytotoxic T lymphocytes. In vitro and in vivo experiments had shown that the vaccine can significantly inhibit the growth and metastasis of CLDN6+ lung cancer cells. Research on the mechanism of action had shown that vaccines reshaped the tumor immune microenvironment, effectively recruiting (through CXCR6) and maintaining the survival and expansion of infiltrating CD8+ T cells by upregulating macrophages expression of CXCL16 and IL-15 through regulating the JAK3/STAT5 signal pathway. In addition, the vaccine demonstrated synergistic anti-tumor effects when combined with PD-1 immune checkpoint blockade therapy. The biosafety assessment showed that it had good biocompatibility.
CONCLUSION: This study developed a nano vaccine platform that integrated targeted delivery, immune regulation, and specific anti-tumor response, providing a new strategy for immunotherapy of CLDN6+ lung cancer.

title: Real-world survival outcomes following multimodal surgical treatment for stage IIIA non-small cell lung cancer.
authors: Carroway WP, Liang E, Jiang SF et al.
abstract:
BACKGROUND: Stage IIIA non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC) is a heterogeneous disease, and the role of surgery within multimodality treatment remains controversial. With the emergence of immunotherapy, there is a need to re-evaluate surgical outcomes in real-world populations. This study compares overall survival (OS) between surgical and non-surgical approaches for stage IIIA NSCLC from a multicenter cohort.
METHODS: We conducted a retrospective cohort study of 598 stage IIIA NSCLC patients diagnosed between January 1, 2010, and June 30, 2021, across 21 Kaiser Permanente Northern California (KPNC) hospitals. Patients were categorized into surgical and non-surgical groups; the surgical group was further divided into surgery alone, surgery first (adjuvant therapy), and surgery later (neoadjuvant or perioperative therapy).
RESULTS: The surgical group had higher 5-year OS (52.6% vs. 30.8%, P<0.001) and longer median survival (5.77 vs. 2.17 years). All surgical subgroups were independently associated with reduced mortality after adjusting for age, sex, body mass index (BMI), smoking status, Charlson Comorbidity Score (CCS), and race: surgery later [adjusted hazard ratio (AHR) =0.50; 95% confidence interval (CI): 0.34-0.74], surgery alone (AHR =0.58; 95% CI: 0.39-0.89), and surgery first (AHR =0.48; 95% CI: 0.37-0.62). Age >80 years (AHR =1.65; 95% CI: 1.07-2.55; P=0.02) and male sex (AHR =1.64; 95% CI: 1.30-2.06; P<0.001) were independently associated with increased mortality.
CONCLUSIONS: Surgery, when integrated into multimodal treatment, is associated with significantly improved survival in stage IIIA NSCLC. These findings support continued consideration of surgery in appropriately selected patients and highlight the need for prospective studies to clarify its role in NSCLC management.

title: Potential to improve early detection of lung cancer through expansion of focused and opportunistic screening approaches: a scoping review focusing on potential expansion of screening risk factors and adoption of artificial intelligence models.
authors: Mok TSK, Finley C, Köksal D et al.
abstract:
BACKGROUND: Low-dose computerized tomography (LDCT) is the gold standard for lung cancer (LC) screening, but access is hindered by strict eligibility criteria and limited infrastructure in low/middle-income countries. A combination of approaches, including expanded screening eligibility criteria and artificial intelligence (AI), could improve detection of early LC in patients excluded by current screening criteria.
AREAS COVERED: A scoping review was conducted (PubMed, Cochrane library, congresses) to explore two potentially complementary approaches to enhance LC screening. The first identified LC risk factors and their potential inclusion in expanded screening criteria, allowing more people at risk to become eligible for screening; the second examined studies involving AI-augmented imaging (CXR or LDCT) to improve workflow, triage, and opportunistic nodule detection.
EXPERT OPINION/COMMENTARY: Several robustly evidenced risk factors for LC were identified that are not included in current screening programs; widening of eligibility criteria could be considered based on local risk profile but requires further research to demonstrate benefit. Opportunistic use of AI-tools to assess incidental chest images may identify patients with pulmonary nodules requiring further investigation but their role in population-level LC screening requires prospective validation in diverse healthcare systems.

title: Who participates in LDCT screening for the early detection of lung cancer after long-term occupational exposure to asbestos dust? Results of the analysis of administrative and medical routine data from the German Social Accident Insurance.
authors: Oubaid N, Greiner F, Keller H et al.
abstract:
BACKGROUND: Lung cancer is one of the most common cancers in Germany and is predominantly detected at an advanced stage. To ensure early detection, the German Social Accident Insurance (DGUV) offers lung cancer screening including a low-dose computed tomography (LDCT) for individuals with long-term occupational exposure to asbestos dust and a smoking history of at least 30 pack years. However, evidence remains scarce about what encourages this group of people to participate in LDCT screening after medical consultation.
METHODS: A secondary data analysis using routinely collected medical and administrative data between 2014 and 2024 was conducted in a cross-sectional design. This study aimed to investigate factors that could be used to predict the uptake of LDCT screening following a medical consultation. Exploratory logistic regression analysis was used to identify and assess possible predictors.
RESULTS: The sample included n = 14,491 individuals (97% male; average age 67 years; average asbestos dust exposure 21 years; average cigarette consumption 43 pack years). 74% of individuals underwent LDCT screening after medical consultation. 13 predictors were included in the regression model. The model demonstrated a low level of variance explanation (Nagelkerkes R2 = 0.026). Younger individuals (OR: 0.96, p < 0.001), individuals with prolonged exposure to asbestos dust (OR: 1.01, p = 0.011) and with a history of pneumonia (OR: 1.16, p = 0.011) were more likely to undergo LDCT screening.
CONCLUSION: The predictors showed only a low explanatory power. Further research should include non-participants and expand the exploratory model to include theoretically grounded predictors.

title: Interstitial Lung Abnormalities: A Multidisciplinary Narrative Review.
authors: Balbi M, Klahr L, Pesci A et al.
abstract: Interstitial lung abnormalities (ILAs) is an umbrella term used to describe a spectrum of computed tomography (CT)-detected lung abnormalities that may reflect interstitial lung disease (ILD). Initially perceived as a niche topic-and often underreported in clinical practice-ILAs have gained increasing attention in recent years, given growing evidence of their association with several adverse outcomes, including increased all-cause, respiratory, and cancer-related mortality. Over time, efforts have been made to standardize the definition, classification, and management of ILAs. The recent American Thoracic Society clinical statement has reshaped the definition of ILAs proposed by the Fleischner Society in 2020, introducing substantial changes to the populations in whom ILAs may be identified and proposing new boundaries to distinguish ILAs from ILD. Nevertheless, several key aspects remain debated, and growing efforts are being made to balance the opportunity for early ILD diagnosis against the risk of unnecessary burden on patients and healthcare systems. This is particularly relevant given the increasing number of CT examinations performed in the general population, as well as in patients at increased risk of ILD, such as those with connective tissue disease, and considering the substantial number of examinations related to expanding implementation of lung cancer screening. In this narrative review, we focus on the definition, implications, and management of ILAs, integrating pulmonology, radiology, and pathology perspectives on the strengths and limitations of current approaches.

title: Association of PET/CT Metabolic Parameters with Histologic Grade of Lung Adenocarcinoma: Implications for Surgical Decisions.
authors: Shen X, Shi H, Wan Z et al.
abstract: Background The grading system for invasive lung adenocarcinoma proposed by the International Association for the Study of Lung Cancer (IASLC) has been widely validated. However, the association of PET/CT with IASLC grade and its value in clinical decision-making is unknown. Purpose To investigate the association of PET/CT metabolic parameters with IASLC grade and determine the complementary clinical value of PET/CT in optimizing preoperative surgical decision-making in clinical stage IA (cIA) lung adenocarcinoma. Materials and Methods This retrospective study included consecutive patients who underwent preoperative PET/CT and complete resection for cIA lung adenocarcinoma between September 2020 and March 2022. Logistic regression was used to identify predictors of grade 3 lung adenocarcinoma. Multivariable Cox models assessed prognostic effects and interactions between maximum standardized uptake value (SUVmax) and surgical strategy. Propensity score matching was used to balance clinicopathologic characteristics across surgical strategies. Results The study included 2789 patients (median age, 62 years [IQR, 55-68 years]; 1574 women). Logistic regression analysis demonstrated a positive interaction between radiologic type and SUVmax (P = .008) in predicting grade 3 adenocarcinoma. Specific cutoff values for pure solid (cutoff of 4.25) and subsolid (cutoff of 2.30) nodules were identified. Positive interactions between SUVmax and surgery were observed exclusively in pure solid nodules (SUVmax-resection extent for overall survival [OS], P = .048; SUVmax-nodal dissection for OS, P = .045). Stratified analyses showed that segmentectomy and limited lymph node dissection were associated with worse outcomes only in hypermetabolic lesions (SUVmax > 4.25; resection extent hazard ratio [HR] for OS, 2.06 [P = .03]; nodal dissection HR for OS, 2.06 [P = .005]). SUVmax maintained robust predictive efficacy for grade 3 lung adenocarcinoma in the external cohort (area under the receiver operating curve, 0.72 for pure solid nodules and 0.74 for subsolid nodules). Conclusion In patients who underwent PET/CT and complete resection for clinical stage IA lung adenocarcinoma, maximum standardized uptake value was an independent predictor of grade 3 lung adenocarcinoma and helped identify high-risk patients treated with segmentectomy or limited nodal dissection. © RSNA, 2026 Supplemental material is available for this article.

title: Oncologic outcomes of sublobar resection in non-small cell lung cancer ≤3 cm with adverse pathologic features.
authors: Yun T, Lee D, Park JH et al.
abstract:
OBJECTIVES: This study evaluated the association between resection extent and recurrence-free survival in patients with clinically node-negative NSCLC ≤3 cm with adverse pathologic features including visceral pleural invasion, spread through air spaces (STAS), or high-grade histology.
METHODS: We retrospectively reviewed patients who underwent curative-intent resection for cN0M0 NSCLC with pathologic tumor size ≤3 cm between 2017 and 2023. Patients were categorized into sublobar resection and lobectomy groups. Cox proportional hazards models were used to identify factors associated with recurrence-free survival. Propensity-score weighting was used to account for measured differences between the surgical groups, followed by weighted survival analyses within prespecified individual and combined adverse-feature subgroups.
RESULTS: Among 1,774 patients, 666 underwent sublobar resection and 1,108 underwent lobectomy. Visceral pleural invasion, STAS, and high-grade histology were independently associated with a higher risk of recurrence. Lobectomy was not independently associated with recurrence-free survival in multivariable analysis (HR, 1.17; 95% CI, 0.69-1.98, p = 0.562). In unadjusted subgroup analyses, recurrence-free survival did not significantly differ by resection extent among patients with visceral pleural invasion, STAS, or high-grade histology with similar findings in combined subgroups (p > 0.05). Weighting reduced the baseline imbalances, while the resulting survival curves remained largely overlapping across the individual adverse-feature subgroups.
CONCLUSIONS: Visceral pleural invasion, STAS, and high-grade histology were independently associated with recurrence, whereas resection extent was not. The weighted analysis did not show a clear separation between surgical groups, although the present analysis was not designed to demonstrate comparable efficacy between the two surgical approaches.

title: External validation of the eurolung risk model for morbidity using an institutional database on minimally invasive major lung resections.
authors: Zhang R, Cheufou D
abstract:
BACKGROUND: The EuroLung1 model was developed by the European Society of Thoracic Surgeons (ESTS) to estimate the risk of major cardiopulmonary complications after anatomical lung resection. Because minimally invasive approaches were underrepresented in the original derivation cohort, its performance in contemporary thoracoscopic practice remains uncertain. We therefore conducted an external validation using a cohort of patients undergoing minimally invasive major lung resection.
METHODS: This retrospective study included 644 consecutive patients (293 females and 351 males; median age, 66 years) treated with thoracoscopic lobectomy or segmentectomy. For each patient, the EuroLung1 score was determined according to the published scoring algorithm incorporating eight weighted clinical and operative variables. Patients were subsequently categorized into the predefined risk classes. Associations between the score and major morbidity were examined, while model discrimination and calibration were evaluated using standard validation metrics.
RESULTS: The cohort included 574 lobectomies (89.1%) and 70 segmentectomies (10.9%). Histopathology revealed 548 patients (85.1%) with confirmed non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC), 66 (10.2%) with benign disease, and 30 (4.7%) with pulmonary metastasis. Postoperative mortality and major complication rates were 0.9% and 12.9%, respectively. In logistic regression analysis, each 1-point increase in the EuroLung1 score was associated with 9% higher odds of morbidity [odds ratio (OR) =1.092, 95% confidence interval (CI): 1.010-1.180, P=0.03]. Similarly, advancing by one risk class conferred a 33% increase in the odds (OR =1.327, 95% CI: 1.027-1.715, P=0.03). Calibration analysis revealed that the EuroLung1 score underestimated morbidity risk in lower-risk classes and overestimated it in higher-risk classes. Discrimination performance of EuroLung1 score was poor, with an area under the receiver operating characteristic (ROC) curve of 0.573.
CONCLUSIONS: Although the EuroLung1 score retained a significant relationship with postoperative major morbidity after minimally invasive anatomical lung resection, its predictive performance was suboptimal. The weak discrimination and variable calibration observed in this validation cohort suggest that model recalibration or revision may be necessary before application to individual risk estimation in contemporary minimally invasive thoracic surgery.

title: Reassessing perioperative risks: impact of neoadjuvant therapy on mortality in pneumonectomy.
authors: Boutros CS, Bassiri A, Jiang B et al.
abstract:
BACKGROUND: The INT0139 trial [2009] raised concerns about the safety of pneumonectomy after chemoradiation due to high perioperative mortality rates. Recent clinical trials have supported the use of neoadjuvant treatment as a viable option for stage Ib or greater lung cancer. We hypothesized that neoadjuvant treatment does not increase perioperative mortality risk in patients undergoing pneumonectomy.
METHODS: Adult patients with nonmetastatic non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC) from the 2004-2021 National Cancer Database undergoing pneumonectomy were analyzed in a retrospective cohort study. Exclusions included missing study variables, non-adenocarcinoma/squamous histology and pneumonectomy after neoadjuvant radiation alone. Multivariate logistic regression analyzed 30- and 90-day mortality and included laterality and neoadjuvant treatment interactions.
RESULTS: Of 14,522 patients, 58.6% underwent right pneumonectomy and 41.4% underwent left pneumonectomy. Neoadjuvant treatment was received by 14.9% (systemic therapy alone: 1,008; systemic therapy + radiation: 1,156). The 90-day mortality was higher for right versus left pneumonectomy (17.2% vs. 9.8%, P<0.001). Neoadjuvant therapy was not associated with higher 90-day mortality compared to surgery alone (10.4% vs. 13%, P=0.04). Independent predictors of mortality included right-sided pneumonectomy [odds ratio (OR) =2.01, 95% confidence interval (CI): 1.78-2.28], advanced age (OR =1.05, 95% CI: 1.04-1.06), and Charlson-Deyo index ≥ 3 (OR =1.98, 95% CI: 1.53-2.57). Interaction analysis showed no increased risk with neoadjuvant therapy for either side.
CONCLUSIONS: This analysis reiterates known elevated risk associated with right pneumonectomy but disputes the dogma that neoadjuvant treatment increases the risk of pneumonectomy, suggesting that neoadjuvant treatment is not a contraindication to receipt of pneumonectomy.

title: Corrigendum to 'Tumor cavitation at durvalumab initiation predicts poor survival in stage III NSCLC after concurrent chemoradiotherapy: A single-center retrospective cohort study' [Respir Investig 64/5 (2026) 101503].
authors: Ota H, Sogabe S, Murakami Y et al.

title: Hypertension and clinical outcomes following thoracic radiotherapy.
authors: McCrohan M, Patel P, Busby T et al.
abstract:
BACKGROUND: Radiation therapy (RT) is highly efficacious in treating thoracic malignancies. However, RT has been linked to potential cardiotoxicity. Yet, the long-term incidence, severity, and implications of HTN-development post-RT are unknown.
METHODS: Leveraging a large US-based Comprehensive-Cancer-Center-cohort of patients treated with thoracic-RT from 2007 to 2019, we included patients ≥18 years old with histologically confirmed esophageal or lung cancers. The primary outcome was incidence of incident/new or worsened HTN [systolic-blood-pressure-(SBP) ≥130 mmHg] after RT-initiation. The secondary outcomes were major-adverse-cardiac-events (MACE- heart-failure, myocardial-infarction, arrhythmia, stroke, and sudden-death), disease-progression, and overall-survival, by HTN-status. Differences in outcomes by HTN-status were also evaluated via landmark-analysis, excluding those with undiagnosed HTN. Observed new HTN rates were compared to Framingham-predicted-rates, and absolute-excess-risks were estimated. Multivariate regression was used to define the relation between clinical and RT measures and both new or worsened HTN-development and survival-outcomes.
RESULTS: Overall, 439 RT-treated patients (238 esophageal; 201 lung; 66.7% male; mean age 63.6 years; 65% baseline HTN) were identified. Over a median follow-up of 23 months, 255 (58.1%) developed new or worsened HTN; median SBP increase of 7 mmHg. In landmark-analysis, the cumulative incidence of new or worsened HTN by 1-year was 48.0% and 63.4%, respectively. Using the JNC-8 cutoff of ≥140/90 mmHg, the new HTN rate was 21.6% at 1-year, translating to a 3.4-fold higher rate than the Framingham-predicted-rate (RR 3.37, P < 0.001). In multivariate regression, RT-dose was consistently associated with new or worsened HTN-development (P < 0.05); those with RT-induced-HTN saw improved progression-free-survival and overall-survival (HR 0.67 and 0.54, P < 0.01, respectively). Beyond traditional factors, only RT-dose is consistently associated with MACE (P < 0.05). No specific antihypertensive class prevented RT-related HTN.
CONCLUSIONS: These data suggest that thoracic-RT increases early HTN risk.

title: Recurrent thymoma-associated PRCA with persistent agranulocytosis: a case report and therapeutic considerations.
authors: Wang A, Xia Y, Xin M et al.
abstract: We report a case of recurrent type A thymoma accompanied by pure red cell aplasia (PRCA) and agranulocytosis. Following local recurrence after thymoma resection, the patient gradually developed anemia and leukopenia as the lesion progressed; bone marrow examination showed marked suppression of erythropoiesis and reduced granulopoiesis. Taken together with the peripheral blood findings, these results suggested thymoma-associated immune-mediated hematopoietic injury. Following multidisciplinary evaluation, the patient underwent thoracoscopic resection of the recurrent lesion, and pathological examination confirmed type A thymoma with negative surgical margins. Postoperative follow-up showed gradual recovery of erythropoiesis and achievement of transfusion independence, whereas agranulocytosis persisted; only after regular cyclosporine A treatment and increased drug exposure did the white blood cell and neutrophil counts gradually rise. Based on this case and previous studies, thymoma resection may reduce immune attack on the bone marrow and create conditions favorable for hematopoietic recovery by removing the source of continued generation and export of abnormal T cells; however, abnormal T cells that have already entered the peripheral blood or bone marrow and continue to survive may perpetuate immune-mediated injury. Therefore, blood counts should be monitored serially after surgery, and standardized adjunctive immunosuppressive therapy should be instituted when necessary. During treatment, close attention should also be paid to medication adherence, therapeutic drug concentrations, and monitoring of hepatic and renal function to balance efficacy and safety.

title: Predictors of pleurodesis success after combined outpatient thoracoscopic talc poudrage and tunneled indwelling pleural catheter placement.
authors: Bani Salem M, Al Zoubi O, Maser T et al.
abstract:
BACKGROUND: Combined ambulatory thoracoscopic talc poudrage and tunneled indwelling pleural catheter (TIPC) placement may facilitate early pleurodesis while preserving outpatient management for malignant pleural effusion (MPE). Predictors of pleurodesis success after this combined approach remain incompletely defined. In this study, we aimed to identify the predictors of successful pleurodesis after this combined approach among patients with expandable and non-expandable lung subgroups.
METHODS: We performed a retrospective cohort study of 100 patients who underwent outpatient thoracoscopic talc poudrage with TIPC placement for MPE. Pleurodesis success was assessed at 3 and 6 months. Multivariable logistic regression was used to identify predictors of success among 97 evaluable patients. Additional analyses were performed in the non-expandable lung subgroup.
RESULTS: Among 97 patients, 77 (79.4%) had expandable lungs. In multivariable analysis, lung expandability was independently associated with pleurodesis success at 3 months [odds ratio (OR), 15.2; 95% confidence interval (CI): 4.22-71.0; P<0.001] and 6 months (OR, 7.97; 95% CI: 2.07-33.9; P=0.003). Cancer group was associated with 3-month success in adjusted analysis (global P=0.046): compared with the lung/mesothelioma group, the other-malignancy group had lower odds of success (OR, 0.19; 95% CI: 0.04-0.73), whereas breast cancer did not differ significantly. No group difference persisted at 6 months (global P=0.46). Lung/mesothelioma-associated MPE had higher early pleurodesis success than other malignancy groups, but not at 6 months. In the non-expandable lung subgroup, complete visceral restriction, airway obstruction and adhesions were associated with lower 6-month pleurodesis success on univariate analysis.
CONCLUSIONS: Lung expandability was the strongest independent predictor of pleurodesis success after combined outpatient thoracoscopic talc poudrage and TIPC placement. Selected patients with non-expandable lung may still achieve successful pleurodesis.

title: Explainable Machine Learning Model for Personalized Assessment of the Need for Intensive Care in Patients with Myasthenia Gravis Based on Phenotype and Inflammatory Markers.
authors: Chang CC, Lin KY, Yeh JH et al.
abstract:
BACKGROUND: Early identification of myasthenia gravis (MG) severe exacerbations that require intensive care unit (ICU) admission remains challenging due disease highly heterogeneous. Existing models seldom incorporate phenotype stratification, limiting interpretability and clinical utility.
AIM: This study aimed to develop an explainable machine learning (ML) model to assess phenotype-specific risk factors and predict ICU admission for patients with MG.
DESIGN AND METHODS: This retrospective study included 319 hospitalized patients with MG. We utilized clinical variables and systemic inflammation markers for ML modeling. Subgroups were prespecified by thymoma status and age at onset. Primary outcome was need for intensive care during the hospitalization. Model performance was assessed. SHapley Additive exPlanations (SHAP) was employed for interpretation of global and individual features.
RESULTS: Of 319 admissions, 33 (10.3%) required ICU care. Four ML models were trained with nested 3-fold validation. eXtreme Gradient Boosting performed best (AUC: 0.94). SHAP ranked MGFA clinical classification, infection during admission, body mass index, and inflammatory indices as principal predictors. Subgroup analyses revealed phenotype-specific patterns, including opposite SHAP directions for inflammatory markers between thymoma and non-thymoma groups and distinct rankings between different age of onset groups. SHAP-based personalized explanations revealed patient-specific variations in risk ranking and directionality of predictive features. A web-based calculator was developed to support real-time clinical implementation of the model, potentially allowing for risk stratification.
CONCLUSIONS: An explainable machine learning framework that integrates clinical features with systemic inflammation indices reliably predicts ICU admission in MG and reveals phenotype-specific risk patterns, enabling personalized risk stratification in MG management.

title: The Expanding Therapeutic Landscape in Myasthenia Gravis.
authors: Rashed HR
abstract: Myasthenia gravis (MG) is a rare autoimmune disorder caused by autoantibodies targeting postsynaptic proteins of the neuromuscular junction. Although conventional therapies can achieve remission or sufficient symptom control in most patients with generalized MG (gMG), approximately 10%-30% of patients remain treatment refractory with an increased risk of myasthenic crises and mortality. In addition, prolonged immunosuppression can cause undesirable side effects. Over the past decade, research has focused on identifying new therapeutic targets, which paved the way to advance the development of novel therapies. Rather than exerting broad immunosuppression, novel therapies selectively target specific components involved in the immunopathogenesis of MG, such as immunoglobulin G (IgG) production (B cell-depleting agents), IgG recycling (neonatal fragment crystallizable receptor, FcRn, blocker), and complement activation (complement inhibitors). Targeted therapies have been evolving exponentially since 2017, marking a new era in treatment strategies in gMG. They have emerged as potential steroid-sparing agents with robust efficacy and favorable safety profiles. Small cohorts have demonstrated the efficacy and tolerability of these therapies during myasthenic crisis and in patients with active thymoma. Although targeted therapies have generally comparable efficacy and safety, treatment plans should be individualized, and several factors should be considered before initiating these therapies, including pharmacological spectrum (complement inhibitors are effective only in acetylcholine receptor antibody-positive MG, while FcRn and B cell-depleting agents have broader spectra), convenience of administration, and cost-effectiveness. This monograph proposes an updated treatment algorithm in refractory gMG that integrates novel targeted therapies alongside standard immunosuppressant steroid-sparing agents.

title: Ligustilide enhances TNTs-mediated mitochondrial transfer to accelerate the reactivation of TECs in sleep deprivation induced postpartum mouse.
authors: Shu Y, Lai X, Xu X et al.
abstract:
ETHNOPHARMACOLOGICAL RELEVANCE: Angelica sinensis (Oliv.) Diels (Danggui) has been widely used by puerperae in China for postpartum recovery for more than a thousand years. Its key active ingredient, ligustilide (LIG), has been documented to exert thymus-repairing effects; however, its role and underlying mechanisms in postpartum thymic regeneration impairment remain unclear.
AIM OF THE STUDY: During the puerperium, the acutely atrophied maternal thymus gradually returns to its non-pregnant state. However, frequent sleep deprivation (SD) resulting from neonatal breastfeeding often slows down the thymus recovery process. This study investigated the efficacy and underlying mechanism of LIG, an active ingredient of A. sinensis, against SD-induced thymic regeneration disorder (SDTRD) in postpartum mice.
MATERIALS AND METHODS: Postpartum SD was induced by automated disturbance; a progesterone-estrogen withdrawal (PE) model followed by a 7-day high-dose steroid treatment. LIG (1 mg/kg) was administered during regeneration. Thymic architecture (H&E), thymic epithelial cells (TEC) localization (immunofluorescence), and thymocyte subsets (flow cytometry) were quantified. Spleen sjTREC, thymic cytokines, and transcripts for mitochondrial biogenesis/function were measured by qPCR. TEM assessed mitochondrial ultrastructure. Dual-color mitochondrial tracing combined with a thymocyte-iTECs co-culture system and a bone-marrow-cell thymic homing assay mapped intercellular mitochondrial transfer. Tunneling nanotubes (TNTs) were disrupted with cytochalasin D; Rho-GTPase activation (including Cdc42) was evaluated.
RESULTS: Postpartum mice with SD showed damaged mitochondrial ultrastructure and reduced mitochondrial biogenesis in TECs, leading to TECs dysfunction and interruption of postpartum thymic regeneration. LIG significantly restored the abnormal spatial localization of TECs, improved the reticular framework of cortical TECs (cTECs), promoted thymocyte development, and increased output of CD4+ T-cells. Mechanistically, LIG may facilitate the formation of F-actin-dependent TNTs between thymocytes and TECs, mediating mitochondrial transfer from thymocytes to dysfunctional TECs. This process may rely on Rho GTPase signaling pathways (Cdc42 activation) to regulate F-actin polymerization.
CONCLUSIONS: LIG may promote F-actin-dependent TNTs-mediated mitochondrial transfer from thymocytes to TECs, thereby reactivating TECs, restoring the thymic microenvironment, rescuing thymocyte development and export, and ultimately ameliorating SD-induced postpartum thymic regeneration. These findings provide new experimental evidence for the development of LIG as a preventive and therapeutic intervention for defective postpartum thymic repair.
